title: Counselor II
description:
Come join our team! At Creative Alternatives you’ll have the opportunity to build a meaningful career while making a lasting difference in the lives of foster youth. We are a mission-driven nonprofit human services agency providing Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program facilities, foster family homes, transitional housing placement, and nonpublic school services for youth and young adults who have experienced significant challenges, trauma and adversity. Every day, our team creates safe, supportive environments where youth can heal, grow, and reach their full potential. As a Counselor II in one of our STRTP facilities, you’ll be more than an employee—you’ll be a mentor, advocate, and positive role model who helps shape brighter futures. If you’re compassionate, dependable, and passionate about helping others, you’ll find purpose, professional growth, and the opportunity to make a real impact with us!

Qualifications:

  • Must meet one of the following:
    • Bachelor of Arts or Science degree
    • Two years’ full-time experience or equivalent, working with population to be served, or equivalent education or experience as determined by CDSS. (Experience shall be verified as having been paid or volunteer with duties that required direct supervision and care of population served.)
  • Prior to assuming duties, individual shall complete a minimum of one hour of training as specified in Section 87065.1(a) in addition to training required in Sections 87065.1(c) and (d)
  • Must be 21 years of age
  • Meet all state licensing and insurance requirements
  • Must pass a DOJ, FBI, and Child Abuse index clearance
  • Valid California driver's license with minimum 2 years’ driving experience required
  • Good driving record: Department of Motor Vehicles printout required
  • Must pass LIC 503 Health Screening Report and TB clearance

Knowledge of:

  • And understanding of the needs of children served in a children’s residential setting

Ability to:

  • Engage and develop a rapport with children who have diverse backgrounds.
  • Provide consistency and behavioral limits through relationship-based interventions.
  • Communicate effectively and solve problems in a collaborative manner.
  • Learn and understand the needs of children served in a residential children’s setting.
  • Develop appropriate relationships with clients who have various backgrounds.
  • Apply the Reasonable Prudent Parent Standard as necessary.
  • Utilize skills in crisis intervention, conflict resolution, and interpersonal communication.
  • Work effectively with staff and administration.
  • Communicate effectively with team members and outside agencies.
  • Implement strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Successfully complete Crisis Prevention Intervention (CPI) post testing course work in emergency intervention and demonstrate “hands on” competency in emergency intervention techniques (per CCL regulation 84802(g), Title 22).

Essential Functions and Responsibilities:

  • Managing the day-to day operation of the facility in the absence of a supervisor.
  • Ensuring appropriate care and supervision is provided to children in according to applicable law, licensing regulations, and the agency’s policies.
  • Supervision, protection, and care of children at all times, individually and in groups.
  • Overseeing the planned activities required to be available to children.
  • Ensuring general upkeep of the facility.
  • Provide mental health services including individual and group rehabilitation services.
  • Write a progress note during each shift for each client.
  • Assistance to each child working with a group and in handling individual problems.
  • Administration of discipline and setting of limits for behavior that are consistent with trauma informed care standards.
  • Notations of the child’s program; identification of the possible need for additional professional services, and communication of such findings to facility supervisor and professional staff.
  • Assistance with the provision of or access to the core services and support, daily activities, and emotional and social supports, as necessary.
  • Reporting to the Facility Supervisor and making recommendations to address identified problems.
  • Applying interventions, techniques, and practices that are trauma informed, culturally relevant, age and developmentally appropriate and consistent with a child’s needs and service plan and treatment plan.
  • Maintain appropriate documentation.
  • Perform various food service and housekeeping functions, including cooking, cleaning and laundry.
  • Transport clients in company vehicles.
  • Participate in crisis intervention as necessary.
  • Complete incident reports as necessary.
  • Participate in staff meetings and training as scheduled.

Physical Demands:

title: Steward for Pastoral Care Ministries
location: 0104 St. Michael Parish, Olympia - Olympia, WA 98501
description:
Position Title: Steward for Pastoral Care Ministries
Reports To: Pastor
Schedule: FTE 1.0 (40 hours per week). Monday–Friday; occasional Saturdays and parish events

Parish Family Description

Through the Partners in the Gospel initiative, the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Seattle has integrated parishes and resources into groupings of parish families that are now in the process of becoming new canonical parishes.

St. Michael Parish and St. Michael Parish School in Olympia, WA comprise a truly vibrant multicultural Catholic community that serves approximately 2,800 families, representing 7,000 individual mass attendees per weekend and approximately 440 school students enrolled in pre-k through 8th grade. The past decade has witnessed unprecedented growth in parish life engagement, ministry participation, and school enrollment.

Saint Edward Parish in Shelton, WA is a diverse parish, inclusive of many ethnic cultures and bilingual function,serving approximately 1200 families per weekend, which strongly suggests vitality for years to come.

Position Summary

The Steward for Pastoral Care provides leadership, coordination, and oversight ministries of compassion, accompaniment, responsiveness, encouragement (C.A.R.E.), across Saint Michael and Saint Edward Parish family. This position ensures that parishioners and members of the wider community receive support during times of illness, grief, disability, loneliness, hardship, and life transition.

Grounded in the Gospel call to “love one another as I have loved you” (John 13:34), the Steward for Pastoral Care develops ministries that foster dignity, belonging, healing, and connection. The role collaborates with parish staff, clergy, volunteers, community organizations, and ministry leaders to strengthen a culture of care and service within Saint Michael and Saint Edward Parish family and the surrounding community.

Parish Family Responsibilities

Eucharistic Visits to the Homebound

  • Coordinate, train, and support Eucharistic Visitors who bring Holy Communion, prayer, and pastoral presence to parish family members who are temporarily or permanently homebound.
  • Provide ongoing formation, communication, and support for Eucharistic Ministers serving in this ministry.
  • Ensure appropriate pastoral follow-up and communication with clergy regarding sacramental needs.

Eucharistic Visits to Patients at Providence Saint Peter Hospital

  • Maintain regular communication and collaboration with the Director of Hospital Spiritual Care, hospital chaplains, and Eucharistic Visitors.
  • Coordinate, train, support, and commission Eucharistic Visitors who bring Holy Communion, prayer, and pastoral presence to parishioners who are temporarily or permanently homebound.
  • Provide ongoing formation, communication, and support for Eucharistic Ministers serving in this ministry.
  • Ensure appropriate pastoral follow-up and communication with clergy regarding sacramental needs.

Compassion Ministry

  • Supervise, train, regularly communicate and assist volunteers.
  • Ensure that no Catholic, or loved one of a Catholic, faces the experience of dying alone.
  • Prepare trained, compassionate parishioners who can accompany individuals and families through serious illness, the dying process, death, and the early period of grief
  • Work closely with the pastor, clergy, Eucharistic Ministers to the Homebound, hospice, hospitals, and other appropriate professionals.
  • Cultivate awareness of accompanying people not simply toward death, but toward Christ.

Phone Call Ministry

  • Supervise, regularly communicate and assist ministry leader and volunteers to ensure every parishioner feels known, valued, and spiritually supported.
  • Supervise program offering phone calls of acknowledgement, prayer, and connection.

Grief Groups

  • Serve as staff contact and coordinator for all grief ministries and gatherings within parish family.

Working Hands

  • Serve as staff contact to coordinate practical assistance for homebound residents through minor home repairs and maintenance.
  • Support projects such as building ramps, repairing appliances, yard work, and other household needs.



Partnership Organizations

  • Chaplains Association for Public Safety - Thurston County (CAPS-TC) serve as staff point of contact for chaplain first responders.

  • Project Rachel Ministry: serve as staff point of contact in supporting women, men, and family members experiencing grief or emotional distress following an abortion by connecting them with confidential Catholic post-abortion healing resources.

Pastoral Care and Community Outreach Commission

  • Collaborate with Steward for Community Outreach to represent the Pastoral Care and Community Outreach Commission in supporting parish decision-making and ministry development.
  • Work closely with commission members in initiatives such as annual grant distribution to community organizations.
  • Provide pastoral insight, ministry coordination, and recommendations for pastoral care and outreach priorities.

Saint Michael Parish: Additional Responsibilities

Support Groups

  • Oversee and support faith-based ministries that provide companionship, healing, and spiritual support for individuals and families experiencing grief, illness, loss, and life challenges.

St. Elizabeth Ann Seton Grief Support

Saturday Mornings, 10:00 am – 12:00 pm (late November – late February)

  • Facilitate weekly meetings and structured grief support cycles
  • Coordinate grief support programs for individuals coping with the death of a loved one, illness, or other significant life challenges
  • Provide group and individual support grounded in Catholic faith and compassion

Monday Evenings, 6:00 – 7:30 pm

  • Supervise, support and stay in contact with group leader; occasionally attend meetings
  • Coordinate regular meetings focused on prayer, encouragement, and accompaniment

St. Peregrine Cancer Support Group

Thursdays, 6:00 – 7:30 pm (in person and via Zoom)

  • Supervise, support and stay in contact with group leader; occasionally attend meetings
  • Support individuals living with cancer, survivors, caregivers, family members, and friends
  • Coordinate prayer, sharing, and support opportunities through in-person and online gatherings

St. Dymphna Dementia and Alzheimer's Support Group

Wednesday Mornings, 10:00 – 11:30 am

  • Supervise, support and stay in contact with group leader; occasionally attend meetings
  • Provide support and resources for families and caregivers of individuals experiencing dementia and Alzheimer's disease
  • Coordinate regular meetings focused on education, prayer, encouragement, and accompaniment

St. Catherine of Siena Miscarriage and Infant Loss Ministry

  • Provide compassionate one-on-one support for individuals and families grieving miscarriage, stillbirth, or neonatal loss

Our Lady of Lourdes Suicide Loss Support Group

Cycles scheduled according to need and request

  • Facilitate 8-week support cycles
  • Provide a safe, faith-based environment for individuals grieving the loss of a loved one to suicide
  • Offer accompaniment, prayer, and resources to support healing and hope

One-to-One Grief Support

  • Provided as needed

All support ministries are rooted in Catholic faith while welcoming people of all religious backgrounds. These ministries provide compassionate peer support and do not replace professional counseling.

Faith and Light: Inclusion & Fellowship

  • Serve as staff contact to support the Faith and Light community, an international ministry that brings together individuals with disabilities, families, and friends for prayer, fellowship, and celebration.
  • Promote inclusion, friendship, and meaningful participation in parish life.

Prayer Shawl Group

  • Serve as staff contact to support volunteers who create prayer shawls while praying for those who will receive them.
  • Coordinate the blessing of shawls by clergy.
  • Supervise distribution of shawls to individuals experiencing illness, grief, hardship, or celebrating significant life moments.

title: Gedragswetenschapper KSO
description:
Werk jij graag met jongeren en krijg je energie van meedenken, adviseren en samen zoeken naar wat een jongere nodig heeft? Heb je affiniteit met verschillende culturen en wil je werken met alleenstaande minderjarige vluchtelingen? Dan maken we graag kennis met je.

Werken op onze KSO-locaties

Op onze KSO-locaties wonen alleenstaande minderjarige vluchtelingen van 15 tot 18 jaar. Jongeren die vaak al veel hebben meegemaakt en in Nederland bezig zijn met het opbouwen van een nieuw leven. Geen jongere en geen verhaal is hetzelfde. Dat maakt het werk afwisselend, maar soms ook complex.

Als gedragswetenschapper sta je dicht bij de dagelijkse praktijk. Je werkt samen met de manager en de woonbegeleiders en denkt mee wanneer een situatie daarom vraagt. Je hoeft niet op afstand mee te kijken, maar bent juist betrokken bij wat er op de locaties gebeurt.

Wat ga je doen?

Je sluit aan bij casuïstiekmomenten en bewoners overleggen en denkt mee met de woonbegeleiders over de begeleiding van de jongeren. Soms gaat het om een vraag over gedrag of ontwikkeling, soms om een situatie waarin zorgen zijn ontstaan of waarin snel geschakeld moet worden.

Je geeft advies, stelt vragen en helpt begeleiders om vanuit verschillende kanten naar een situatie te kijken. Samen zoek je naar wat op dat moment passend is voor de jongere.

Je houdt je onder andere bezig met:

· aansluiten bij casuïstiekmomenten en bewoners overleggen;

· adviseren en ondersteunen van woonbegeleiders bij vragen en complexe situaties;

· meedenken over de begeleiding en ontwikkeling van jongeren;

· ondersteunen bij het opstellen en evalueren van begeleidingsplannen;

· ondersteunen bij het maken van een veiligheidsplan wanneer dat nodig is;

· samenwerken met jeugdbeschermers en andere betrokken ketenpartners;

· waar nodig afstemmen met andere partijen rondom een jongere;

· meedenken bij situaties waarin de veiligheid of het welzijn van een jongere onder druk staat;

· ondersteunen bij crisissituaties en helpen om op zulke momenten de juiste stappen te zetten.

Het werk is soms onvoorspelbaar. Een crisissituatie houdt zich immers niet altijd aan kantoortijden. Daarom zoeken we iemand die flexibel is, snel kan schakelen en het prettig vindt om samen met de locatie naar een oplossing te zoeken.

Wie zoeken we?

We zoeken vooral iemand die nieuwsgierig is naar jongeren en hun achtergrond. Iemand die niet meteen een oordeel klaar heeft, maar wil begrijpen waar gedrag vandaan komt en wat een jongere nodig heeft.

Daarnaast:

· heb je een afgeronde WO-opleiding in de orthopedagogiek, psychologie of een vergelijkbare richting;

· heb je affiniteit met het werken met jongeren;

· heb je interesse in verschillende culturen en achtergronden en werk je cultuursensitief;

· kun je goed samenwerken en tegelijkertijd zelfstandig je professionele advies geven;

· ben je flexibel en kun je goed omgaan met onverwachte situaties;

· kun je makkelijk schakelen tussen verschillende betrokken partijen;

· is ervaring als gedragswetenschapper een pré.

Wat bieden we jou?

Je gaat voor 18 uur per week aan de slag, waarbij we de werkdagen en uren in overleg met de manager afstemmen.

Je werkt grotendeels samen met de woonbegeleiders en hebt daarnaast veel contact met de manager en andere betrokken professionals. Je krijgt de ruimte om jouw kennis en ervaring in te zetten en verder te ontwikkelen binnen het werken met deze bijzondere doelgroep.

Verder bieden we:

· een salaris in schaal 11 volgens de cao Jeugdzorg;

· 8% vakantietoeslag;

· een eindejaarsuitkering van 8,3%;

· een goede pensioenregeling;

title: Senior Software Developer
description:
About Contour


Contour Software has grown from a dozen people to over 2,000 staff across 3 cities, in less than 14 years.

As a subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc., we are proud to be part of a global enterprise software conglomerate that has grown to become one of the top 10 software companies in the world, with employees and customers in 100+ countries. With a broad-based and ever-growing portfolio of market-leading, vertical-market enterprise solutions covering more than 100 industry domains in predominantly mature markets, CSI's recipe creates the perfect environment for professionals to build fulfilling, long-term careers.

What started as an R&D & Accounting back-office, has progressed into a full-service Global Centre serving all functions and departments, at the divisional as well as operating group/corporate level. Today Contour employees, located in Karachi, Lahore & Islamabad, are serving CSI divisions located in time zones spanning the globe, from Sydney to Vancouver. With the global growth of Constellation as the wind in our sails, we are only just getting started!

Role summary

We're hiring a senior developer for our Desktop team. The team owns our current desktop products, which are Windows applications built on Visual Basic 6 (VB6) and COM, and which customers depend on every day, while CalcAir builds modern web versions of those products.

This is a lasting senior role for an engineer who knows VB6 deeply and uses AI tools to understand, document, and safely improve existing code. Our desktop products will stay in service for as long as customers depend on them, and you'll help keep them reliable, make the team's day-to-day work smoother, and help plan the path from VB6 to the web.

We're adopting an AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) approach, where AI takes on more of the analysis and building while engineers set direction, review the work, and make the decisions that matter. You'll work with our Desktop Team Lead and the Desktop team, with Product, and with Infrastructure & IT on builds and releases.
What you'll accomplish in your first year

  • First 90 days: Learn our VB6 codebase and the business rules behind it. Use Claude Code to map the highest-risk areas and document how they work. Get comfortable with our GitHub and Azure DevOps (ADO) workflows, and note where the team's process creates the most friction.
  • By 6 months: Add tests around critical workflows so changes are safer. Lead a set of fixes or improvements from planning through release, using AI-DLC checkpoints. Make the first improvements to how we build, test, and release. Share practical AI techniques for legacy code with the team.
  • By 12 months: Help define the path from our VB6 products to the web, including which business rules to carry forward and which to rebuild. Deliver the first meaningful piece of that work, and keep improving how the team works along the way.


Responsibilities

Desktop product support

  • Lead the technical work on VB6 desktop products, including defect fixes, enhancements, and releases.
  • Serve as the senior technical resource for hard problems and critical customer issues.
  • Keep current products stable, supportable, and documented for as long as customers depend on them.

Process and workflow improvement

  • Find and fix the slow, manual, or error-prone steps in how we build, test, and release desktop products.
  • Improve how we use GitHub and Azure DevOps (ADO), so work is tracked, reviewed, and released consistently.
  • Use Claude Code to automate repetitive work in analysis, testing, and documentation.
  • Turn what works into shared team practices, so the whole team benefits.

Legacy code understanding and modernization

  • Use Claude Code to analyze VB6 code: map workflows, extract business rules, and identify risk before changes are made.
  • Write and maintain characterization tests that capture current behavior, so the web versions can be checked against it.
  • Work with Product to decide which business rules and behaviors carry forward into the web products.

AI-assisted development

  • Use Claude Code as a regular part of your daily work for analysis, changes, tests, and documentation.
  • Apply AI-DLC practices and help the Desktop team use AI safely on legacy code.
  • Review AI-generated changes carefully, especially in code with little test coverage.

Collaboration and delivery

  • Work in GitHub for source control and pull requests, and in Azure DevOps (ADO) for work items and tracking.
  • Partner with Infrastructure & IT on builds, releases, and environments.
  • Mentor Desktop team members and document what you learn, so it isn't held by one person.

Required qualifications

  • 6+ years of professional software development, including substantial production work in VB6.
  • Deep understanding of Windows desktop application architecture, data access, and debugging VB6 applications.
  • Strong working knowledge of the COM model, ActiveX components, the Windows registry, and how legacy 32-bit applications behave on modern Windows systems.
  • Experience reading and documenting large legacy codebases, and turning them into clear descriptions of how things work.
  • Daily, hands-on use of Claude Code or a comparable agentic coding tool, with examples you can walk us through.
  • A working understanding of AI-DLC and how it applies to legacy work.
  • Experience with GitHub and Azure DevOps (ADO).
  • A track record of improving team processes and workflows, such as build, test, and release steps, and making the changes stick.
  • Senior-level judgment: you can weigh risk, explain tradeoffs to non-technical leaders, and say when something should wait.

Nice to have

  • Experience migrating VB6 or other legacy Windows applications to .NET or the web.
  • Experience with .NET/C#, React, or SQL Server, to help with the path to the web.
  • Experience writing characterization or regression tests for legacy systems.
  • Experience building AI-assisted workflows for a team, such as custom skills, agents, or MCP integrations.
  • Experience with Azure DevOps (ADO) pipelines.

Exciting Benefits we offer:

  • Market-leading Salary
  • Medical Coverage – Self & Dependents
  • Parents Medical Coverage
  • Provident Fund
  • Employee Performance-based bonuses
  • Home Internet Subsidy
  • Conveyance Allowance

title: AI Security Researcher
description:
About Cogent

Cogent is an Applied AI Lab building the next generation of AI agents for cybersecurity. AI has fundamentally changed how attacks happen, allowing malicious actors to operate at unprecedented speed and scale. Cogent's "AI Taskforce" assesses petabytes of enterprise data to remediate these issues before critical breaches occur.

To stay at the cutting edge, we blend frontier research with real-world execution. Alongside our core product work, Cogent Research serves as our applied AI lab, providing the research horsepower needed to make truly agentic security workflows a reality. We partner with Fortune 500 companies to secure some of the most complex production environments in the world.

We're backed by Greylock & Bain Capital Ventures, and we've built a team with the best minds in applied AI. Our team is comprised of people from:

  • Top universities like Stanford, Berkeley, Penn, Duke, Carnegie Mellon, Waterloo

  • Unicorn, high-growth companies like Scale AI, Databricks, Stripe, Tesla, Coinbase

  • World class cybersecurity experts from Wiz, Abnormal AI, Zscaler

  • Preeminent research labs like Deepmind and SAIL

About the Role

We're hiring a Security Researcher to build the offensive side of our research - the attacker our defensive agents have to beat. You'll sit in Research and own the loop that turns real red team tradecraft into AI capability, shaping how offensive expertise becomes autonomous capability rather than just supplying the expertise.

What You'll Do

  • Design and build our red team agents. Architect the agent harness, the tools and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers they call, and the skills that encode how an operator actually works - from scoping and reconnaissance through payload development, delivery, Command and Control (for example Mythic), and post-exploitation toward the objective - turned into repeatable, agent-executable capabilities for our offensive agent and VR-1. You'll review the agents' runs and close the gaps.

  • Push the agents to full-chain operations across every surface. Our red team agent covers application and code security today. You'll drive its extension into full attack chains - initial access, delivery and evasion, Command and Control, privilege escalation, and lateral movement - across Windows, Active Directory, and on-prem, and work with our cloud security researchers to extend coverage into cloud (identity and access management, misconfiguration, continuous integration and delivery) and network.

  • Own the evasion and tradecraft edge. Build detection-evasion know-how into the agents and test harness, and the detonation and detection loop that validates it against real Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR). This is what lets our defensive agent train against a real adversary instead of a toy.

  • Design and operate the cyber ranges this runs in. Build realistic environments with real defenses in place (EDR, Security Information and Event Management, logging), stood up in-house and via vendors like Ludus - Windows and Active Directory-heavy to start, extending to cloud and hybrid alongside the cloud security team. These are where agents are trained, benchmarked, and verified.

  • Build the benchmarks that prove the agents improved. Turn attack paths into evaluation tasks with verifiable success criteria, feeding benchmarks like IntrusionBench, so we can measure whether each change actually makes the agents better.

  • Verify critical and high-severity attack paths in real customer environments, and feed what you learn back into the agents and detections.

  • Represent Cogent in the offensive security community through research, talks, and open-source contributions.

What We're Looking For

  • 6+ years of experience in offensive security, red team operations, or adversary emulation

  • Hands-on operator who has run full-chain operations end-to-end - initial access through post-exploitation - across Windows, Active Directory, and on-prem environments

  • Depth in Command and Control frameworks (for example Mythic) and payload development, with real detection-evasion experience against EDR

  • A builder who writes code (for example Python) to turn manual tradecraft into repeatable, automatable capability rather than one-off operations

  • Experience standing up and operating realistic test environments or cyber ranges with production defenses in place (EDR, SIEM, logging)

Bonus Points

  • Cloud (identity and access management, misconfiguration, CI/CD) or network attack experience

  • Experience building evaluations or benchmarks that measure security capability

  • Open-source tooling, conference talks, or published research in offensive security

  • Experience working with AI agents, LLM tooling, or agentic workflows

title: Software Developer
description:
LSEG (London Stock Exchange Group) is more than a diversified global financial markets infrastructure and data business. We are dedicated, open-access partners with a dedication to excellence in delivering the services our customers expect from us. With extensive experience, deep knowledge and worldwide presence across financial markets, we enable businesses and economies around the world to fund innovation, manage risk and create jobs.

If you're looking for a new challenge where you can stretch and develop your technical skills, this could be the opportunity for you. We'd love to hear from you!

Role Purpose

Index Process Automation is an in-house technical team within FTSE Russell Operations. As Senior Software Developer, you will be a key member in helping shape and build the future of technology for FTSE Russell Operations. Project work is critical to enhancing quality, growing coverage, improving service and operational resiliency, and increasing automation. Primary responsibilities of the team include centralizing automation, innovation, and research to design, develop, and implement process improvements and simplification. This role will help enable transformational change across the FTSE Russell Operations global team.

Python developer with react front-end and Python backend experience, you will be responsible for developing and helping maintain our AWS hosted web application. Collaborate with data modelers, analysts, and business users to ensure ongoing development with different product teams.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the demonstration of adherence to the LSEG Data standard policies and procedures.
  • Adapt quickly to new technologies, tools, and frameworks as needed for projects.
  • Engage in continuous learning to stay updated with industry trends and best practices.
  • Develop and maintain web applications using React and Python.
  • Write clean, maintainable, and efficient code.
  • Optimize applications and code for speed and scalability.
  • Fix and debug applications to improve performance.
  • Participate in code reviews and contribute to teams’ best practices.
  • Document data ownership and establish integrations with enterprise data repositories.
Skills & Experience:
  • Proven experience of a python developer with 3+ years in an enterprise environment.
  • Solid understanding of OOP principles, experience using common libraries for data manipulation (pandas, NumPy, datetime, regex functions).
  • 2+ years of front-end development with experience in React, JS, HTLM, and CSS.
  • 1+ years of experience in SQL Server writing basic queries and executing SP’s.
  • Knowledge of version control systems (e.g. Git we use Bitbucket, GitLab)
  • Experience in creating comprehensive documentation using systems like Confluence and bug tracking software like Jira.
  • Proficient in using testing frameworks (unit test, pytest, Jest) to ensure code quality and maintainability.
  • Desirable: Hands-on experience with AWS, AZURE, or other cloud providers. Experience with databricks, adf, glue, ETL’s, and ELT’s.
  • Demonstrated ability to work inclusively, communicate effectively, and collaborate within a team, ensuring a collaborative and productive work environment.
Soft Skills
  • An enthusiastic advocate of high-quality solutions
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with ability to communicate technical information to non-technical partners and to listen to identified concerns and adapt accordingly

Career Stage:

Senior Associate

London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) Information:

Join us and be part of a team that values innovation, quality, and continuous improvement. If you're ready to take your career to the next level and make a significant impact, we'd love to hear from you.

LSEG is a leading global financial markets infrastructure and data provider. Our purpose is driving financial stability, empowering economies and enabling customers to create sustainable growth.

Our purpose is the foundation on which our culture is built. Our values of Integrity, Partnership, Excellence and Change underpin our purpose and set the standard for everything we do, every day. They go to the heart of who we are and guide our decision making and everyday actions.

Working with us means that you will be part of a dynamic organisation of 25,000 people across 65 countries. However, we will value your individuality and enable you to bring your true self to work so you can help enrich our diverse workforce.

We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer. This means that we do not discriminate on the basis of anyone’s race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. Conforming with applicable law, we can reasonably accommodate applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs.

You will be part of a collaborative and creative culture where we encourage new ideas. We are committed to sustainability across our global business and we are proud to partner with our customers to help them meet their sustainability objectives. Our charity, the LSEG Foundation provides charitable grants to community groups that help people access economic opportunities and build a secure future with financial independence. Colleagues can get involved through fundraising and volunteering.

LSEG offers a range of tailored benefits and support, including healthcare, retirement planning, paid volunteering days and wellbeing initiatives.

title: Portfolio Management Analyst I- Global Fund Banking
description:
Overview

This is a hybrid role, with the expectation that time working will regularly take place inside and outside of our Phoenix office.

First Citizens Bank helps personal, business, commercial and wealth clients build financial strength that lasts. Headquartered in Raleigh, N.C., First Citizens has built a unique legacy of strength, stability and long-term thinking that has spanned generations. First Citizens offers an array of general banking services including a network of more than 550 branches in 23 states and commercial banking expertise delivering best-in-class lending, leasing and other financial services coast to coast. Parent company First Citizens BancShares, Inc. (NASDAQ: FCNCA) is a top 20 U.S. financial institution with more than $200 billion in assets.

First Citizens Fund Banking, formerly SVB Global Fund Banking, is a premier fund finance partner to venture capital and private equity firms. With more than 40 years of experience, we deliver a comprehensive set of banking and lending solutions, valuable market insights, and curated industry connections to the most prestigious firms.

The Portfolio Management team is responsible for the timely and accurate processing of loan advances and paydowns as well as compliance reporting documentation review.

The Portfolio Management Analyst I is responsible for executing risk management controls for the Global Fund Banking lending portfolio. Core responsibilities include ensuring borrower compliance and availability for straight-forward loan advances, timely tracking and review of expected statements from borrowers, and other loan maintenance tasks. Performs client outreach for advance and payment status updates and request clarifications. Coordinates approval from Senior Credit Officers for draws requested from uncommitted balances. Navigates a comprehensive set of procedures, accurately identifying and executing correct protocol for each situation. This role includes regular interaction with multiple Global Fund Banking teams as well as many other Business Partners throughout the bank.


Responsibilities & Qualifications

Duties & Responsibilities:

Bachelor’s degree with 1 year of professional office/banking experience or High School diploma/GED with 2 years of experience

Preferred:

  • Proficient with Microsoft Office with an emphasis in SharePoint Online - experience pulling and analyzing data for reporting purposes
  • Proficient in navigating and applying procedural frameworks, able to escalate issues and follow-up appropriately
  • Strong organization and analytical skills in addition to the ability to work independently
  • Strong critical thinking, proactive and desire to collaborate with team
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills to engage with business partners, leadership and clients on email and phone
  • Can develop strong working relationships with internal teams
  • Strong ability to multi-task job functions on high volume days, attention to detail
  • Adaptability in fast-paced, evolving environments

Position Specific Skills:

Business analytical skills

Communication (written and verbal)

Adaptability


Additional Information

Benefits are an integral part of total rewards and First Citizens Bank is committed to providing a competitive, thoughtfully designed and quality benefits program to meet the needs of our associates. More information can be found at https://jobs.firstcitizens.com/benefits.

title: Yard Tech - AZ
description:
SUMMARY

We are seeking a reliable and hardworking Yard Technician to join our team. This position involves managing yard operations, including moving equipment, cleaning the yard, assisting with receiving and shipping, and preparing units for transport. The ideal candidate will have excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced environment.

Responsibilities:

The following responsibilities are a general guideline and not intended to be an exhaustive list of the full scope of responsibilities. Duties and responsibilities are subject to change based on business needs and at management’s discretion.

  • Safely move and relocate equipment around the yard as needed using forklifts, trucks, and other equipment.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment by performing regular yard cleaning duties.
  • Assist with receiving shipments, inspecting goods, and ensuring the proper documentation is completed.
  • Prepare units and equipment for shipping, including loading, securing, and verifying that all items are properly packaged.
  • Assist in unloading and staging incoming deliveries, ensuring they are placed in the correct location in the yard.
  • Coordinate with team members to ensure efficient yard operations and effective use of space.
  • Perform routine maintenance and checks on equipment and yard tools.
  • Follow safety protocols and company procedures to minimize accidents and risks.

title: Director, US Immigration
description:
Overview

At KPMG in Canada, our people bring their unique perspectives to Canada’s most important challenges. Here, you can build momentum that reaches beyond our business, develop skills for the future, and take ownership of your career with support at every stage. Join a firm where your career can make a difference.

KPMG Law LLP is a national law firm affiliated with the professional services firm of KPMG LLP, with offices in major markets across Canada. As an integrated, multidisciplinary firm, our lawyers work closely with accountants and other professionals on complex client engagements across a broad range of legal and tax-related practice areas.

KPMG Law LLP’s Immigration Law practice is looking for an experienced US immigration attorney to join at the Director level. In this senior role, you will provide strategic advice on complex US business immigration matters, lead client engagements and relationships, and contribute to the continued growth of the practice.

As a Director, you will act as a trusted advisor to clients, taking ownership of complex US immigration matters and providing practical, business-focused legal advice. You will develop senior client relationships, identify opportunities to expand those relationships, mentor members of the immigration team, and strengthen the visibility and growth of KPMG Law’s US Immigration practice.


What you will do

  • Advise clients on complex US business immigration matters, including non-immigrant visas, PERM, immigrant petitions and adjustment of status matters
  • Lead complex client engagements from initial strategy through delivery, providing practical legal advice aligned with clients’ broader business and workforce needs
  • Develop and manage senior client relationships, identify opportunities to broaden our support to clients, and contribute to the continued growth of the U.S. Immigration practice.
  • Manage client proposals, define the scope of engagements, and coordinate related engagement activities.
  • Oversee a high volume of immigration matters while maintaining quality, responsiveness and compliance with applicable requirements
  • Mentor and coach lawyers and other members of the immigration team, providing technical leadership on complex and evolving areas of US immigration law
  • Monitor legislative, regulatory and policy developments and advise clients on implications for their organizations and employees
  • Contribute to thought leadership, client alerts and presentations, and collaborate across KPMG Law and the broader KPMG organization to identify opportunities to serve clients across disciplines

What you bring to the role

  • Law degree from an accredited institution and admission to a US state Bar in good standing
  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain any authorization required by the Law Society of Ontario to provide advice in Ontario regarding US law, including a Foreign Legal Consultant permit, as applicable
  • A minimum of 12 years practising corporate US business immigration law, advising clients on complex immigration matters.
  • Significant experience leading corporate US immigration programs
  • Deep technical knowledge of US business immigration, including non-immigrant visa matters, PERM, I-140 petitions and I-485 applications
  • Experience with employment-based and family-based consular immigrant visa applications
  • Proven ability to independently lead complex client engagements and provide strategic, business-focused legal advice
  • Strong track record of developing senior client relationships, identifying business development opportunities and contributing to practice growth
  • Experience mentoring and coaching legal professionals, combined with strong legal writing, analytical and communication skills and the ability to manage multiple complex matters in a high-volume environment

Providing you with the support you need to be at your best


Our Values, The KPMG Way

Integrity, we do what is right | Excellence, we never stop learning and improving | Courage, we think and act boldly | Together, we respect each other and draw strength from our differences | For Better, we do what matters

KPMG in Canada is a proud equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating a respectful, inclusive and barrier-free workplace that allows all of our people to reach their full potential. A diverse workforce is key to our success and we believe in bringing your whole self to work. We welcome all qualified candidates to apply and hope you will choose KPMG in Canada as your employer of choice.

Adjustments and accommodations throughout the recruitment process

At KPMG, we are committed to fostering an inclusive recruitment process where all candidates can be themselves and excel. We aim to provide a positive experience and are prepared to offer adjustments or accommodations to help you perform at your best. Adjustments (informal requests), such as extra preparation time or the option for micro breaks during interviews, and accommodations (formal requests), such as accessible communication supports or technology aids, are tailored to individual needs and role requirements. You will have an opportunity to request an adjustment or accommodation at any point throughout the recruitment process. If you require support, please contact KPMG’s Employee Relations Service team by calling 1-888-466-4778.

AI Usage

We embrace the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance the candidate experience and streamline our recruitment processes. AI tools may help with organizing applications or surfacing relevant qualifications. However, no hiring decisions are made using AI. Every hiring decision is made by our hiring managers and recruitment professionals, who are equipped with training that empowers them to use these tools responsibly. AI technologies used in our recruitment process undergo detailed risk assessments, including security and privacy requirements, that align with KPMG’s Trusted AI framework.

We believe technology should empower human judgment, not replace it. It’s one of the many ways we’re delivering on our vision of being a technology-first, people-driven firm.

title: Hardware Operations Program Manager
description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders, soldiers in battlefield scenarios, and beyond.

About the role:

Skydio is seeking a talented, multi-disciplinary program manager to drive successful delivery of new product & sustaining projects within the Operations organization. In this critical role your contributions will directly impact quality, speed to market, productivity, scaling of manufacturing operations, and profitability as Skydio delivers revolutionary autonomous drones and infrastructure to market, building advanced hardware with modern techniques in an American factory.

How you'll make an impact:

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with product, engineering, reliability, customer service, supply chain, logistics, manufacturing and production teams to plan and execute the detailed development, implementation and support of new hardware products.

  • Define objectives, deliverables & metrics for projects with clear exit criteria for each program phase to meet schedule, cost, quality and capacity targets. Run internal operations and production readiness meetings.

  • Plan projects & programs, track progress, communicate status and escalate issues, leading risk management and problem-solving as appropriate throughout the program lifecycle.

  • Drive program review meetings, partnering with cross-functional program managers to provide concise and actionable status updates, solicit critical input, and communicate risks.

  • Develop & improve processes for supply chain, manufacturing and quality, ensuring operations deliverables are completed on time for successful project outcomes.

  • Coordinate & prioritize post-ramp qualification and sustaining activities including product improvements, international expansion, transition to and from contract manufacturers, engineering builds, system-level testing, ECO implementation, and end-of-life planning.

What makes you a good fit:

  • Functional understanding of manufacturing, quality, supply chain, engineering and change management throughout the product development lifecycle

  • Strong electro-mechanical program management background, preferably with consumer and industrial electronics

  • Excellent problem-solving, critical thinking, organizational, communication and leadership skills

  • Analytical approach to drive recommendations based on data, identifying or developing tools to coordinate and track project progress

  • Willingness to work outside the scope of your role to cover gaps in ownership

  • Ability to remain flexible, calm and creative in the face of uncertainty and change

  • Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions

Compensation: At Skydio, our compensation packages for regular, full-time employees include competitive base salaries, equity in the form of stock options, and comprehensive benefits packages. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. Relocation assistance may also be provided for eligible roles. The annual base salary range for this position is $170,000 - $200,000*. Fundamentally, we believe that equity is the key to long-term financial growth, and we ensure all regular, full-time employees have the opportunity to significantly benefit from the company's success. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to enroll in the Company’s group health insurance plans. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to receive the following benefits: Paid vacation time, sick leave, holiday pay and 401K savings plan. This position and all associated benefits are subject to applicable federal, state, and local laws, as well as the Company’s policies and eligibility criteria.

*Compensation for certain positions may vary based on the position’s location.

title: Security Program Manager
description:
Loudoun County Government has been named one of Forbes' 2025 Best Large Employers! We’re proud to be recognized nationally for our commitment to employee satisfaction and excellence in public service. At Loudoun County, we bring together talented professionals from all backgrounds to make a meaningful impact in a dynamic, growing community — that’s The Loudoun Difference.

Welcome and thank you for your interest in employment with Loudoun County Government!

ALL SECTIONS OF THE APPLICATION MUST BE COMPLETED IN ITS ENTIRETY. THE RESUME IS CONSIDERED SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION ONLY. APPLICATIONS THAT ARE INCOMPLETE OR INDICATE 'SEE RESUME' WILL NOT BE TAKEN INTO CONSIDERATION.


_________________________________________________________________________________________

Introduction

Loudoun County Office of Emergency Management, Safety & Security is seeking a detail-oriented, innovative, and analytical team player for a Security Program Manager position. An ideal candidate should be a known problem-solver, collaborator, and effective communicator, and thrive in a fast-paced, result-oriented environment. This position provides leadership and oversight of service areas; markets program services to stakeholders and community; oversees program budget and delivery of program services; maintains compliance with policies, procedures and processes, related laws, regulations, ordinances, best practices, and industry standards; maintains program records and analyzes programmatic return on investment.

Job Summary

This position reports directly to the Safety and Security Program Administrator and is responsible for, but not limited to, the following duties:

  • Responsible for program management to include defining goals, objectives, and performance metrics; ensuring services are delivered efficiently and effectively; along with personnel management to include day-to-day supervision, coaching, and mentoring.
  • Assists with the development and management of division budget and contract management.
  • Ensures the development and delivery of required training programs; consults with stakeholders; represents the organization at internal and external meetings and conferences; and serves on local, regional, or state committees and working groups.
  • Manages the development, implementation, and maintenance of facility emergency plans and associated training and drills.
  • Manages the lifesaving and life-sustaining equipment deployed to County facilities.
  • Organize and maintain program and project documents, reports, and information.
  • Responds to urgent situations at County facilities to assist with the implementation of plans, policies, procedures, and processes. Assigned to leadership/support positions within the Emergency Operations Center during activation.
  • Manages the County’s respiratory protection program and equipment in accordance with applicable standards, laws, and regulations.
The ideal candidate will be a highly effective communicator capable of conveying complex information in a clear and concise manner; have the ability to develop, implement, and maintain a variety of plans, policies, and procedures in the programmatic area of health and safety; maintain an understanding of applicable Occupational Health and Safety standards and regulations; and possess the skills requisite to provide day-to-day supervision, professional development, coaching and mentoring of assigned personnel.

Hiring salary is commensurate with experience.

Minimum Qualifications

The Security Program Manager position requires a bachelor’s degree in workplace safety and security, occupational safety, or a related field; five (5) years of related work experience including one (1) year of supervisory or team lead experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Job Contingencies and Special Requirements

This position requires a valid driver’s license. Successful candidates will undergo background checks as required.

title: Project Analyst I
description:
Short Description

Bowman has an opportunity for a Project Analyst I to join our team in Charlotte, NC.

At Bowman, we believe in creating opportunities for aspiring people to thrive and achieve ambitious goals. That’s why a career at Bowman is more than a job. It is an opportunity to be part of a diverse and engaged community of professionals, to be treated as a respected and valued member of a motivated team and to be empowered to do exceptional work that advances the best interest of everyone involved. We recognize the importance of creating a work environment that is both rewarding to our employees and supportive of our unwavering commitment to provide unparalleled service to our clients.



Purpose

Manage and coordinate the administrative aspects of projects to ensure they are completed on time and within budget. Support Project Manager by analyzing data and contributing to overall project strategy and performance evaluation.



Responsibilities

Leadership and Direction

  • Receive general instruction on key objectives for execution. Receive direction as needed, and especially complex assignments, modified techniques, and new approaches on assignments with conflicting criteria. Work is completed using advanced techniques and principles and is reviewed by more senior staff to ensure application of sound professional judgement. May review work produced by junior staff for quality assurance.

At the Operational and Company Level

  • May act as key point of contact for interdepartmental communications for a branch office, Business Unit / Service line.
  • In conjunction with Marketing, may support aspects of proposal preparation and contract pricing.
  • Assist project managers and local / Business Unit management team with revenue projections and budgeting.
  • Act as liaison between the management team and other technical staff, as needed.
  • Proactively communicate with internal and external constituents, acting as administrative point of contact for client.
  • Provide operational support to stakeholders by tracking timelines and ensuring project goals are being met.
  • Provide support in developing and improving internal processes while supporting strategic and tactical planning and execution.
  • May manage platforms and systems related to project development and management of the branch office, Business Unit / Service line.

Do the Work

  • Support principals, project managers, and team leads with planning and executing technical projects, including monitoring project schedules, reporting, cost estimates and budgets, and tracking of team activities.
  • Create and maintain project documentation, including timelines, resource plans, and meeting minutes. Prepare presentations and ongoing status reports.
  • Research, monitor, and analyze data to provide insight and recommend action if necessary.
  • Assist local management team in preparing production schedules and project budgets.
  • Assist in responding to Requests for Proposal (RFP), ensuring compliance with requested requirements.
  • Coordinate multiple projects concurrently.
  • Monitor and communicate project progress and scope to key constituents and adapt to changes.
  • Review all project contractual documents for conformity and quality assurance.
  • May assist Accounting in providing and/or reviewing monthly billing information.
  • Work closely with Accounting to maintain project information in Bowman’s accounting systems.
  • May assist Accounting with collection efforts.
  • Using past metrics, work closely with management and Marketing on proposals and contracts for prospective projects.
  • Work to streamline operational processes through SOPs, software development, etc.


Success Metrics and Competencies

  • Ability to work both independently and within a team environment.
  • Ability to effectively communicate with all levels of the organization and external partners.
  • Highly motivated and problem-solving attitude.
  • Strong sense of urgency in responding to constituents.
  • Strong work ethic and commitment to quality.
  • Self-reliance and ability to operate independently with limited direction.
  • Commitment to promoting the reputation of the company through quality of work.
  • Aspirations to grow professionally and advance within the company.
  • Commitment to driving profitability and growth.
  • Commitment to becoming a “citizen” of the broader organization, breaking down barriers and silos.
  • Commitment to working in partnership with others inside and outside the organization.
  • Ability to effectively manage multiple time-sensitive tasks.
  • Thorough understanding of data analysis techniques and deliverables.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to summarize conclusions and confidently present well-supported arguments with internal/external stakeholders.
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and time management skills needed to meet deadlines.
  • Ability to synthesize complex information, coordinate and manage multiple projects, and multitask and prioritize deadlines demonstrated by work experience and/or academic record.
  • Ability to compose professional business-related correspondence, accurately proofread documents and read, interpret and understand Civil and Architectural Drawings.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships.


Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration or related field preferred, or equivalent commensurate experience.
  • Entry level position, no prior experience required. Any professional experience is a plus.
  • Knowledge of project management from conception to delivery.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and web browsers (Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome).
  • Proficiency in Adobe and/or Bluebeam a plus.
  • Familiarity with Deltek and PandaDoc a plus.
  • Project Management certification(s) or progress towards such certifications preferred (PMP, CAPM, CSM, CompTIA, etc.)


About Bowman

Are you ready to build a career that makes a lasting impact? At Bowman, our people are at the center of everything we do. We’re committed to creating an environment where employees can thrive both personally and professionally, while helping to shape the infrastructure of tomorrow.

A career at Bowman means being part of a collaborative, forward-thinking organization where innovation, inclusion, and growth are encouraged at every level. We offer competitive compensation, a supportive work environment, and benefits designed to help our employees succeed.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes:

  • Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance
  • 401(k) retirement savings plan with company match
  • Paid time off, sick leave, and paid holidays
  • Tuition reimbursement and professional development support
  • Discretionary bonuses and other performance-based incentives
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP), wellness initiatives, and employee discounts

Eligibility for certain benefits may vary based on position, location, and employment status.



Physical Demands and Working Environment

  • May be eligible for hybrid or remote work arrangements.
  • Primarily indoor professional office environment which may include bright/dim light, noise, fumes, odors, and traffic.
  • Mobility around an office environment.
  • Frequent and prolonged use of standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines.
  • Occasional local travel during the business day, although some out-of-the-area and overnight travel may be required according to the needs of the business.
  • Occasional lifting or carrying up to 20 pounds.
  • Occasional pushing or pulling up to 20 pounds.
  • Occasional reaching outward or above shoulder.

title: Full Stack Software Engineer
description:
Are you a full-stack engineer who enjoys solving complex technical challenges and building solutions that make data more accessible and useful?

We’re looking for a Full-Stack Software Engineer to join our Document Analytics team and help build modern, secure, and scalable technology solutions.

In this role, you’ll work across the full software development lifecycle, from solution design and hands-on development through testing, deployment, troubleshooting, and production support. You’ll build user-facing applications, APIs, integrations, and data-driven capabilities that help connect users with meaningful information and analytical insights.

This is a highly collaborative role where you’ll partner with engineers, architects, analytics professionals, product teams, operations, designers, and business stakeholders to turn real business needs into reliable technical solutions.

What You’ll Do
  • Design, build, and maintain modern full-stack applications using React, TypeScript/JavaScript, HTML, and CSS on the front end.
  • Develop reliable, scalable, and secure backend services using Go, C#, and/or Java.
  • Design and develop RESTful APIs, services, and integrations that enable access to data and analytical capabilities.
  • Build and maintain efficient database solutions, including working with PostgreSQL/Postgres and other data technologies.
  • Partner with product managers, architects, engineers, and business stakeholders to translate requirements into effective technical solutions.
  • Collaborate with UX/design partners to deliver intuitive, high-quality user experiences.
  • Assess technical requirements, recommend solution options, and provide reasonable development and delivery estimates.
  • Troubleshoot complex application and production issues and contribute to effective root-cause resolution.
  • Develop unit and integration tests to maintain application reliability and code quality.
  • Participate in code reviews, pair programming, and other collaborative engineering practices.
  • Work with Kubernetes and cloud-native technologies to support scalable application deployment.
  • Use modern development tools, including GitHub Copilot, to improve engineering productivity and quality.
  • Continuously explore new technologies and development practices that can improve our products and engineering environment.
What We’re Looking For
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 3+ years of professional software engineering experience.
  • Demonstrated experience building both front-end and back-end applications.
  • Strong hands-on experience with React and JavaScript/TypeScript, along with HTML and CSS.
  • Professional backend development experience using at least one of the following: Go/Golang, strongly preferred C#/.NET Java
  • Experience designing, developing, and consuming APIs and web services.
  • Experience working with Kubernetes and containerized applications.
  • Solid understanding of software engineering principles, application architecture, testing, and maintainable code.
  • Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, including experience investigating and resolving complex technical issues.
  • Ability to evaluate requirements, recommend technical approaches, and estimate level of effort.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams.
  • A continuous-learning mindset and willingness to challenge existing approaches constructively.
Nice to Have
  • Hands-on experience with Go/Golang in production environments.
  • Experience with PostgreSQL/Postgres or comparable relational databases.
  • Experience with Microsoft Azure and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) or other cloud platforms such as AWS or Google Cloud.
  • Knowledge of DevOps and CI/CD practices.
  • Experience with Git/GitHub and modern source-control practices.
  • Experience with engineering and project-tracking tools such as Jira.
  • Experience developing data-intensive, analytics, or document-processing applications.
What Success Looks Like

You’ll bring genuine full-stack engineering capability, comfortably moving between a modern React front end and backend services and APIs. You’ll be someone who can take a problem from requirements through implementation, testing, and production, while collaborating closely with the people around you.

Most importantly, you’ll be curious, pragmatic, and motivated by building technology that is secure, scalable, maintainable, and useful.

When You Join Our Team
  • We’ll empower you to learn, grow, and build the career you want.
  • You’ll work in a collaborative environment where different perspectives and ideas are valued.
  • You’ll have opportunities to work with modern technologies and contribute directly to meaningful engineering challenges.
  • As part of a global team, you’ll help shape technology solutions that support the future of the organization.

At Fanshawe College, we're transforming how students learn through extended reality (XR), immersive technologies and artificial intelligence (AI). As an Immersive Technology Specialist, you'll do more than support technology, you'll help design, build, and implement cutting-edge learning and research experiences that impact thousands of students across multiple disciplines.


From developing XR applications and supporting advanced simulation environments to collaborating with faculty, researchers, and industry partners, you'll have the opportunity to explore emerging technologies while helping prepare the next generation of talent.

Position Summary:


The Immersive Technology Specialist, reporting directly to the Director, Immersive Technologies and Simulation, plays a crucial role in facilitating the seamless integration, utilization, and development of immersive technologies and experiences at Fanshawe College. This pivotal position involves collaborating with academic departments, Information Technology Services, faculty members, researchers, and instructional designers, while also maintaining immersive technology equipment, ensuring up-to-date applications, and facilitating the onboarding of faculty, staff, and students. The incumbent enhances the implementation and support of cutting-edge immersive technology research and learning experiences.

Content Development and Innovation

Curriculum Integration and Support, Professional Development and Networking, and Other Duties as assigned

title: Manager Collections Recovery
description:
Overview

PenFed is hiring a Manager Collections Recovery to work onsite at our San Antonio, Texas Service Center. The primary purpose of this role will be to drive the strategy of the unit and ensure corporate strategic initiatives are supported, and that processes are aligned with division targets in an efficient and effective manner. The role will also provide oversight and management of entire consumer charge-off portfolio including debt sales, 3rd party assignment of charged off loans and in-house charge-off recovery activity. The incumbent will oversee the day-to-day operational process of the recovery unit within Collections.


Responsibilities

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. This is not intended to be an all-inclusive list of job duties, and the position will perform other duties as assigned.

  • Manage and develop a team consisting of recovery specialist, recovery analyst and team lead ensuring all internal standards are met in a compliant manner in accordance with applicable federal/state regulations, guidance, and established standard levels of service.
  • Implement performance management through developed score card system and team KPI’s providing coaching and feedback on at least a monthly basis.
  • Oversee the assigned tasks and unit employees to include recruitment, scheduling, capacity, task completion, performance evaluations, KPI’s/Goals, and provide guidance on recovery related issues acting as a SME expert for the work of your unit.
  • Identifies training and cross training opportunities for recovery collections staff as appropriate and implement training/development plans to alleviate single point of failure.
  • Determine and implement succession plans as appropriate.
  • Apply QC methods to ensure records all recovery activity in the appropriate collection systems, documenting the status of defaulted loans and follow up continually for pertinent documentation as required.
  • Drive success of recovery unit and assigned personnel by consistently mentoring staff in individual and team performance, department policies and procedures, productivity, quality, job knowledge, and innovation while tracking capacity.
  • Oversee pipeline management of internal recovery on consumer loans ensuring adherence to regulations, compliance, Q/A, and set internal recovery process.
  • Oversee recovery analyst work ensuring that all work performed is free of defect and timelines/SLAs are met.
  • Oversee vendor performance and determine adjustments in strategy based on results.
  • Ensure the review and creation of accurate reporting including daily, weekly and monthly recovery reports, consolidating and interpreting various reports including portfolios that are serviced by collection agencies ensuring that goals are met or exceeded.
  • Use data to identify trends, implement forecasting and model out projections to meet business needs.
  • Develop and maintain a complete repository of all policies, procedures, process maps and controls that govern the work performed by the charge-off recovery unit.
  • Provides effective communication and service to members, department staff, vendors, attorneys, court systems, and other departments.
  • Collaborates with multiple lines of business for any updates/changes that may cause impact, including partnering with legal, compliance and business risk.
  • Keeping abreast of all industry trends related to recovery collections staying informed of new ideas and developments through publications, membership in professional organizations and contact with other financial institutions.
  • Drive and implement continuous improvement through identifying areas for improvement, implement automation and technology enhancements and driving projects that will increase overall efficiency.
  • Review competitive market practices and provide recommendations to Senior Leadership concerning adjustments to programs in related areas.
  • Participate in business unit and corporate initiatives as assigned to include coordinating and conducting team meetings regularly to review current credit union initiatives, performance results of unit or organization, and coordinate and/or provide training or re-training on credit union procedures and technical processes.
  • May manage other charge-off collection processes as business dictates.

Qualifications

Equivalent combination of education and experience is considered.

  • Bachelor’s Degree in related field required.
  • Minimum of eight (8) years’ experience in collections with a focus on asset recovery and pipeline management required.
  • Minimum of three (3) years’ supervisor / management experience required.
  • Requires experience in managing multiple teams/functions and building relationships with people at a variety of levels.
  • Knowledge of the roles, skills and technical knowledge required to achieve goals within the relevant technical discipline.
  • Strong leadership capability includes interpersonal skills, mentoring, coaching, collaborating, and team building.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Effective time management, problem solving and multi-tasking skills.
  • Effective presentation skills with experience delivering data to various management levels.
  • Strong knowledge of technologies, analytics, methodologies, and practices in the relevant discipline.
  • Experience with A.I. tools preferred.

Supervisory Responsibility

This position will supervise employees.

Licenses and Certifications

Collection Association Certification preferred.

Work Environment

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to an indoor office setting with moderate noise.

*Most roles require working in an office setting with moderate noise and the ability to lift 25 pounds.*

Travel

Ability to travel to various worksites and be on call is required.

title: Software Engineer, Sales Systems
description:
Netic is the AI revenue engine for essential services who are the backbone of the American economy. With $43M in funding from Founders Fund, Greylock, Hanabi, and Dylan Field who led our Series B, we helped our customers book hundreds of thousands of jobs across services industries in North America. There are now companies operating entirely AI-first on Netic.

You’ll join our team with relentless builders from Scale, Databricks, HRT, Meta, MIT, Stanford, and Harvard in bringing frontier AI to the physical economy, where the problems are hard, the data is complex, and the impact is immediate and tangible.

The role

You'll be the first engineer dedicated to Netic's go-to-market systems. There's no GTM architecture to inherit: you'll decide how Salesforce, billing, product data and the warehouse fit together, set the technical direction, and build the platform our sales, ops and finance teams run on.

This is a senior, high-ownership role. You'll treat the GTM stack as a product, decide what to build and what to buy, and bring the same AI-first approach we bring to our customers. As the team grows, you'll help hire and mentor the engineers who join it.

What you'll do

  • Own the architecture of the GTM stack: how Salesforce, billing and finance systems, product data and the data warehouse connect, so a deal flows from first touch to invoice without manual re-entry.

  • Set the technical roadmap with Sales Ops, Deal Desk and the GTM Data Analyst, and decide what to build, buy or retire.

  • Automate sales ops workflows end to end: lead and account routing, territory assignment, approval flows, quote-to-cash and commission inputs.

  • Build internal tools and AI agents that remove manual work for reps and ops, such as account research, call prep, data enrichment and Salesforce hygiene.

  • Own the reliability, observability and correctness of GTM data pipelines, with monitoring that catches a broken sync or a wrong dashboard before a user does.

  • Set engineering standards for the GTM stack: version control, testing, CI/CD and documentation for Salesforce and the services around it.

  • Help hire and mentor the engineers who join the team.

What success looks like in year one

  • A documented GTM architecture and roadmap that leadership has signed off on.

  • Lead-to-cash running without manual re-entry, with data reconciled across Salesforce, billing and the warehouse.

  • AI tooling in daily use by reps and ops, with time saved measured.

  • Salesforce and GTM services under version control, tested and deployed through CI.

What you bring

  • 5–7 years of professional software engineering experience, including senior ownership of production systems.

  • A track record of designing systems end to end and leading projects from scoping to release with little oversight.

  • Strong skills in Python or TypeScript, plus SQL.

  • Deep experience integrating with Salesforce (REST/Bulk APIs, Apex, Flows or platform events) or similar business systems.

  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS or GCP), event-driven pipelines and workflow orchestration.

  • An owner's mindset and care for data correctness, plus the ability to turn vague problems from non-technical stakeholders into shipped solutions.

Nice to have

  • Experience as the first engineer on an internal tools or business systems team.

  • Experience building with LLMs and agent frameworks.

  • Experience with NetSuite, Stripe or another billing system, CPQ, or a reverse-ETL tool (Hightouch, Census).

  • Experience with data infrastructure such as dbt, Airflow or Snowflake.

Our values

  1. Obsess over the customer

  2. Every second counts

  3. Sweat the details

  4. There are no blockers

  5. Be self-directed

  6. Seek and speak the truth

  7. Enjoy the ride

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status.
