title: Senior Manager, Software Engineering (Data Architecture)
description:
Passionate about precision medicine and advancing the healthcare industry?

Recent advancements in underlying technology have finally made it possible for AI to impact clinical care in a meaningful way. Tempus' proprietary platform connects an entire ecosystem of real-world evidence to deliver real-time, actionable insights to physicians, providing critical information about the right treatments for the right patients, at the right time.

About Tempus

Tempus is on a mission to create the world’s largest integrated dataset of clinical and molecular data. We believe that, through data, we can make a lasting contribution to cancer research and treatment. At Tempus, products are owned and developed by small, autonomous teams of developers, designers, data scientists, and product managers who work together to build a platform that is both nimble and innovative.


The Role

As Senior Manager, Software Engineering, you will lead and mentor a small team of data engineers and data architects, and you will own the enterprise data model and the reliability of the data it represents. You will design how clinical records, genomics, next-generation sequencing (NGS) laboratory data, and radiology data are integrated, and you will ensure that the data are accurate, traceable, and suitable for critical applications such as machine learning and clinical decision-making.

You will establish modeling standards, implement quality gates in data pipelines, and develop the team through design review, code review, and ongoing coaching. You will use development tools assisted by artificial intelligence (AI) to accelerate design, testing, and delivery.


What You Will Do
  • Lead and mentor a small team of data engineers and data architects by conducting design and code reviews, providing technical guidance, and fostering a culture of excellence in data architecture and data quality.
  • Own and evolve an enterprise data model with engineers, product managers, scientists, and operators, integrating structured data from clinical records, genomics, the NGS laboratory, and radiology across relational and NoSQL data stores. Author and maintain entity-relationship diagrams, data dictionaries, API specifications, and data-translation documentation at the conceptual, logical, and physical levels.
  • Apply modern data architecture best practices and patterns, and teach modeling standards, including third normal form, dimensional (star schema) design, and established healthcare data model standards such as FHIR, OMOP, and related standards.
  • Evaluate the completeness of source-system models and partner data through profiling, and resolve structural inconsistencies before they reach downstream consumers.
  • Design observability for the data ecosystem with BigQuery, dbt, Elementary, and Grafana, including monitors, alerts, dashboards, lineage, and traceability back to source systems.
  • Partner with product managers and engineering leads to prioritize the backlog, estimate work, and translate complex requirements into actionable technical tasks. Advance the use of AI-assisted development, including Cursor, Claude, and GitHub Copilot, to accelerate modeling, testing, refactoring, and pipeline development.

Why We Are Looking for You
  • You have a record of leading and mentoring a small team of data engineers and data architects, of setting standards, and of guiding design in a fast-paced environment. You can translate gaps in the data model and in data quality into clear recommendations for engineers, scientists, and other stakeholders.
  • You are an expert in the modern data stack, particularly dbt, SQL, and Python, and you have demonstrated exceptional SQL skills in an enterprise data warehouse. You are proficient in the use of AI coding assistants such as Cursor, Claude, and GitHub Copilot.
  • You have applied modern data architecture best practices and patterns, and you can guide a team in their use. You have strong experience with third normal form (3NF) and dimensional (star schema) modeling; with established healthcare data model standards such as FHIR, OMOP, and related standards; and with modeling tools such as Erwin, Vertabelo, or Lucidchart.
  • You understand ETL/ELT and business intelligence (BI) architectures, and you can explain the long-term implications of choosing among relational, massively parallel processing (MPP), and NoSQL technologies. You have architected solutions across more than one of these technologies.
  • You have practical experience with data observability (for example, Elementary and Grafana) and with profiling and correlation analysis to identify data-integrity problems.
  • You have domain experience in healthcare and next-generation sequencing, including clinical and genomic data.

Preferred
  • Deep knowledge of Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and BigQuery architecture.
  • Experience modeling NGS data output.
  • Experience in implementing master data, reference data, or metadata management.

Why Join Tempus

You will work at the intersection of software engineering and cancer research. In this role, you will lead a small team of data engineers and data architects and shape the data model and quality systems that make Tempus data reliable enough for research and clinical use.

$150,000 - $225,000


The expected salary range may vary for other locations. Actual salary may vary based on qualifications and experience. Tempus offers a full range of benefits, which may include incentive compensation, restricted stock units, medical and other benefits depending on the position.

title: Research Engineer / Scientist, World Models & Robot Learning
description:
Help robots understand what happens next.

Dynamic Creatures builds interactive character robots for entertainment and hospitality. We are looking for a hands-on researcher or engineer to develop visual world models that help robots understand their surroundings, anticipate how situations evolve, and use those predictions to guide behaviour.

The role centres on learning from images, video and robot interaction data. You will investigate representations of the physical world, predictive and action-conditioned models, and the connection between visual understanding and robot policies. Experience with vision-language-action models is particularly relevant.

What you will do

• Build and evaluate visual world models that capture scene dynamics, object interactions and the effects of robot actions.

• Develop models and representations from video and robot data, including self-supervised learning and action-conditioned prediction where appropriate.

• Connect learned representations and predictions to planning, policy learning and robot behaviour in collaboration with robotics and controls engineers.

• Own experiments from data collection and curation through model training, evaluation and validation on physical systems.

• Design evaluations that test predictive accuracy, generalisation, robustness and usefulness for downstream robot tasks.

• Investigate failures, improve data and models, and address inference latency and compute constraints.

What we are looking for

• Substantial hands-on experience in world models, video representation learning, predictive modelling or closely related robot-learning research.

• Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with personal ownership of model training and evaluation.

• A strong foundation in computer vision, deep learning and temporal or sequential modelling.

• Evidence of rigorous experimentation: clear baselines, meaningful evaluations, and an ability to explain what worked, what failed and why.

• Interest in translating research into capabilities on real robots, working closely with engineers across perception, autonomy and control.

Particularly useful experience

• Action-conditioned video or latent dynamics models, self-supervised visual representations, or model-based planning.

• Vision-language-action models, imitation learning or reinforcement learning.

• Training on robot demonstrations and interaction data, and deploying learned systems on physical robots.

• Efficient inference, distributed training or large-scale video and robotics datasets.

We welcome relevant experience from industry, academic research or substantial independent work. A PhD is welcome but is not a requirement where equivalent research and engineering depth is demonstrated.

Please apply with your resume and, where available, a paper, repository, project or short demonstration. Tell us what you personally built, how you evaluated it and whether it has run on physical hardware.

location: Seattle, Washington, USA; New York, New York, USA; San Diego, California, USA; Sunnyvale, California, USA
description:
ABOUT US

E-commerce got real-time data infrastructure decades ago. Physical stores still have not. RADAR is changing that.
RADAR is building the data infrastructure layer for the physical world, starting with retail. Our hardware-enabled SaaS platform uses proprietary overhead sensors, software, and AI-powered analytics to locate every product in a store, continuously, down to the fixture. We are deployed across 1,500+ stores with retailers including American Eagle Outfitters and Old Navy, processing tens of billions of real-world events every day, delivering 99%+ accuracy in complex, noisy environments - at fleet scale.
RADAR is one of the best-funded companies in retail technology, backed by a recent Series B financing at a $1 billion valuation. Inventory accuracy is only the beginning. We believe RADAR can become foundational infrastructure for the physical economy, powering new AI-driven commerce experiences across retail and beyond.
Join us if you want to work on a large, unsolved, technically challenging problem with an ambitious team building category-defining technology.

OUR VALUES
  • Mission-Driven: We're transforming retail with cutting-edge technology and building something that truly matters.
  • Collaborative Team: We thrive on curiosity, shared goals, and solving complex problems together.
  • High Impact: You’ll make meaningful contributions from day one and help shape the future of our product and company.
  • Clear Communication: We value honesty, humility, and respectful dialogue—everyone’s voice matters.
  • Balanced Lives: We work hard, but not at the expense of well-being. We respect time, boundaries, and life outside of work.
  • Diverse Perspectives: We believe better ideas come from diverse backgrounds, experiences, and viewpoints.
  • Empathy-Driven Design: We build with deep respect for our end users, listening closely to their feedback and needs.

ABOUT THE JOB

We’re looking for a Staff iOS Engineer to shape Radar’s mobile and cross-platform technical strategy and influence engineering direction well beyond the iOS team. We’re redesigning and rebuilding our mobile apps from the ground up, and you’ll be the technical leader shaping it. This is a senior individual contributor role with no formal management duties. You’ll lead through deep technical expertise, sound judgment, and influence. You’ll work with significant autonomy to set long-term architecture, drive innovation, and guide major cross-functional initiatives with product, design, Android, platform, and backend leaders. You’ll stay hands-on in the code while multiplying the impact of engineers across the organization.

Responsibilities:
  • Define the multi-year mobile architecture and technical strategy.
  • Co-lead cross-platform strategy, including shared code and Kotlin Multiplatform adoption, in partnership with Android and backend leaders.
  • Drive innovation by finding new technical bets and platform capabilities that open up product opportunities.
  • Guide major cross-functional initiatives across mobile, platform, and backend teams from concept to measurable outcome.
  • Stay hands-on: design and build the most complex, highest-leverage parts of the iOS codebase in Swift and SwiftUI.
  • Set engineering standards for architecture, quality, performance, and reliability, and get them adopted across teams.
  • Mentor Staff and Senior engineers and help grow Radar’s next generation of technical leaders.
  • Help drive the technical vision and architecture as we rebuild Radar’s mobile apps, a rare chance to define the foundation of our next-generation product.
  • Plan and drive the migration of existing customers from legacy apps to the new app, keeping the experience smooth and low-risk with minimal disruption.
  • Keep supporting and improving Radar’s legacy products, balancing their stability and customer needs against investment in the new platform.
ABOUT YOURequired:
  • You have extensive experience building and shipping iOS applications, including setting the technical direction for large-scale, widely used apps.
  • You have deep expertise in Swift, SwiftUI, UIKit, and Apple platform internals, including concurrency, performance, and memory management.
  • You have set technical strategy across multiple teams or an organization, with clear influence on product and business outcomes.
  • You have led major, multi-quarter initiatives across functions and delivered measurable results.
  • You are able to define your own priorities and problem space with little direction, and you work with a high degree of autonomy.
  • You are skilled at influencing without authority and can get senior engineers and leaders aligned on complex technical decisions.
  • You are an excellent communicator who explains complex tradeoffs clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • You are a proven mentor to senior engineers and a multiplier who raises the bar for everyone around you.
  • You are energized by ambiguity and high ownership in a fast-moving startup.
Preferred:
  • You have worked as a Staff+ engineer, or in an equivalent technical leadership role, at a company through a period of significant scale.
  • You have led a major app rewrite or re-platforming and migrated existing users to it successfully.
  • You have hands-on experience with Kotlin Multiplatform or other cross-platform code-sharing approaches on iOS.
  • You have experience with modular app architecture, and build-system optimization
  • You have shipped features using newer Apple capabilities such as widgets, Live Activities etc.
  • You are passionate about design detail, accessibility, and delightful user experiences.
  • You have experience developing and shipping a configurable UI
  • You have experience building iOS apps on gRPC and Protocol Buffers, including API contract design, streaming, and network performance tuning.
WHAT YOU'LL DOIn your first 30 days, you will:
  • Learn Radar’s mission, technology stack and core values.
  • Complete onboarding and security compliance training.
  • Meet engineering, product, design, and leadership stakeholders to understand company priorities, and ship your first production change.
In your first 60 days, you will:
  • Get familiar with Radar’s legacy apps: their architecture, customer usage, and technical debt.
  • Make significant contributions to a feature in the rebuilt app.
  • Lead architecture and design reviews and begin mentoring Staff and Senior engineers.
In your first 90 days, you will:
  • Deliver measurable progress on the rebuild, with core foundations in place and the team building on them.
  • Contribute to a new feature in the legacy app, keeping it valuable to customers.
  • Get engineering standards and best practices adopted across multiple teams.
  • Become a go-to technical authority across Radar whose input shapes key product and engineering decisions.

At RADAR, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. The expected base salary range for this position is $172,000 - $250,000. Individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience and relevant education or training.You will also be eligible to receive other benefits including: equity, comprehensive medical and dental coverage, life and disability benefits, 401k plan, flexible time off, and paid parental leave. title: Theater-Based Flight/Ground Test Engineer
description:
Overview

Theater-Based Flight/Ground Test Engineer

LOCATION: Huntsville, AL, Redstone Arsenal

JOB STATUS: Full-time

CLEARANCE: SECRET

TRAVEL: Up to 20%

Astrion has an exciting opportunity for a Theater-Based Flight/Ground Test Engineer supporting the Missile Defense Agency’s Theater-Based Defense Directorate (TB), THAAD Test (TBTT) division at the Von Braun Complex on the Redstone Arsenal in Huntsville, Alabama. Astrion is at the forefront of new missile defense technologies and supports the MDA’s rigorous operational and developmental testing. This exciting, rewarding work helps guarantee the security of the United States and our Allies. Join a professional team of highly qualified engineers, analysts, scientists, and technicians supporting the research, development, testing, and evaluation of the missile defense system whose purpose is to detect, track, engage, and destroy adversary missiles.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS / SKILLS

  • MS in a related engineering field. A BS with five years of additional relevant experience may be substituted for the MS degree requirement
  • 10 years of recent relevant experience
  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain at least a Secret security clearance
  • Experience working in a fast paced, professional team environment with the ability to adjust/react to short notice requirements changes, deadlines, changing schedules, competing priorities, and unpredictable events
  • Strong oral and written communications skills
  • Must be willing to travel up to 20% of the time

HIGHLY DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS / SKILLS

  • Keen understanding of the systems engineering processes from requirements development to verification and testing
  • Familiarity with Missile Defense Agency program objectives
  • In depth knowledge of the Missile Defense System (MDS) capability, components and system level topics
  • Knowledge of MDA test planning, processes and execution
  • Experience with development of test plans (Test Evaluation Master Plan (TEMP) or Integrated Master Test Plan (IMTP)) for major defense acquisition program
  • Experience in planning test events in a resource constrained environment
  • Experience with cybersecurity test planning
  • Hardware in the Loop test experience
  • Experience in development of briefings for Sr. Leadership
  • Recent experience in THAAD development of Hardware and Software components.
  • Experience modeling threat ballistic missiles and/or analyzing threat data in any or all of the following disciplines: Auto CAD, LabView, MS Office, DEWEsoft, Python
  • Proficient with Windows-based PC software (e.g. Word, PowerPoint, Excel, MS Project, MS Teams)

RESPONSIBILITIES

The Flight/Ground Test Engineer plays a critical role in the integration, execution, and continuous improvement of the THAAD weapons system within simulated and live wargaming environments. Their duties span the full lifecycle of test events, divided into Non-Deployed (Lab & Training) and Deployed (Operational Execution) responsibilities which include:

  • Support system readiness, software validation, and personnel training within the laboratory environment
  • Monitor systems to identify deficiencies, annotate issues, and recommend practical fixes
  • Develop and present comprehensive briefings for visiting VIPs to demonstrate the operation use and strategic impact of RISTS within the WG&E ecosystem
  • Manage end-to-end execution of Flight Test and wargames and exercises, from initial scenario design to post-event analysis
  • Design realistic, challenging wargame scenarios – define core objectives, manage logistical parameters
  • Provide Warfighter information to build high-fidelity end-to-end digital representations of the THAAD weapons system constructing robust battle plans, and Flight Test scenarios
  • Integrate RISTS into the broader BMDS architecture
  • Instruct and educate military audiences on threat tactics, system capabilities and employment methodologies
  • Support operational execution by managing and operating complex simulation systems and conduct real-time assessments of simulated engagements
  • Provide analysis and reporting of event outcomes
  • Provide exceptional downrange support, which is instrumental in the successful execution of THAAD Flight tests.
  • Provide proven, step-by-step process flows, product enhancement across all mission areas, and application of critically protected information criteria and lessons learned, and full compliance with all applicable DoD/MDA directives.
  • Support technical efforts for the THAAD systems case involving the integration, checkout, and delivery of THAAD battery equipment, including supporting Element Integration and Checkout (EICO) of each THAAD battery at test ranges.
  • Support the pre-test planning, development of test documentation, range coordination, site preparation, management reviews, test execution, data collection, and data transfer activities.
  • Coordinate with the THAAD Program Office and DE in development of TO memos, test scenarios, test requirements, and test range logistics.
  • Support executive reviews/brief-outs to apprise leadership of mission status, including preparing for/participating in CVTCs from remote test range locations and developing executive-level technical briefings (e.g., for THAAD UAE EICO-A/TrackEx EMER).
  • Support all Continuous Development Integration (CDI) activities on behalf of the THAAD Ground Test Directorate (THTG)
  • Review and provide inputs to MDA Test Objective Memorandums (TOM), Operational Tasking Link (OPTASKLINK), and Event Communications Baseline (ECB)
  • Support MDA Ground Test Directorate (DTG) Executive and Integrated Test Team (IETT) Reviews
  • Develop inputs to MDA Ground Test Source material including event Scenario Matrices (SM) and Scenario Design Reviews (SDR) for the MDA Directorate for Test (DT)
  • Develop Test Readiness Reviews (TRR) and brief to the THAAD Weapon System Test (THT) Director
  • Lead the MDA and THAAD Quality teams through the Certification Data Package (CDP) Process, confirming M&S HW/SW readiness for testing
  • Lead all phases of Ground Test Development from Element Standalone (ESA) to Test Case Integration (TCI) and Developmental/Operational Test Runs-for-Record (DT/OT RFR)
  • Interface with THAAD Warfighters (WF) regarding their roles, event scenarios, and TTP/PPR for MDA Ground Test events
  • Observe Laboratory M&S system performance, WF interaction, and submit daily End-of Day (EOD) reports during MDA Ground Test events RFR
  • Develop Test Execution Reports (TER) including anomaly investigation and analysis along with formal System Test Observation (STO) status and reporting

title: Staff Engineer
description:
About LG Ad Solutions

LG Ad Solutions is a global leader in connected TV (CTV) and cross-screen advertising. We deliver innovative advertising solutions that integrate seamlessly with today’s evolving digital media landscape, powering targeted advertising, measurement, and data-driven decision-making across our global CTV ecosystem.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to join our engineering team in Bangalore, India. In this role, you will drive the architecture, design, and development of large-scale ad serving, measurement, targeting, and data engineering systems that power LG Ad Solutions’ global advertising platform.

As a senior technical leader, you will own critical technical initiatives spanning multiple engineering teams, establish architectural direction, and drive the delivery of highly scalable, reliable, and cost-efficient distributed systems. You will work closely with engineering, product, and operations teams across geographies, providing technical leadership and collaborating with teams in the US and India to deliver high-impact solutions.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role for an engineer who combines deep software engineering expertise with strong architectural judgment, a track record of solving complex engineering problems, and the ability to influence technical decisions across teams. You will also mentor senior engineers, establish engineering best practices, and help shape the long-term technical roadmap of LG Ad Solutions.

Responsibilities

  • Technical Leadership and Architecture: Define and drive the architecture of large-scale, distributed software systems, making critical technical decisions around scalability, reliability, performance, and maintainability.

  • System Design and Scalability: Design and evolve high-throughput ad serving, targeting, measurement, and data processing systems capable of handling large data volumes and demanding latency requirements.

  • End-to-End Technical Ownership: Lead complex, cross-team engineering initiatives from problem definition and requirements gathering through architecture, implementation, deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement.

  • Distributed Systems and Data Engineering: Drive the design and optimization of big data applications and distributed computing platforms, improving processing efficiency, resource utilization, and infrastructure cost.

  • Technical Strategy and Roadmap: Partner with engineering leadership and product teams to define technical strategy, identify architectural gaps, establish long-term roadmaps, and align engineering investments with business priorities.

  • Engineering Excellence: Establish and champion best practices for software design, code quality, testing, observability, operational readiness, and production reliability.

  • Cross-Team Influence: Collaborate across engineering teams and organizational boundaries to resolve complex technical challenges, align architectural decisions, and drive consistent engineering standards.

  • Mentorship and Technical Development: Mentor senior and junior engineers, guide design and code reviews, and help develop technical leadership within the organization.

  • Performance and Reliability: Identify and resolve system bottlenecks, improve service-level objectives, and lead initiatives that enhance throughput, latency, fault tolerance, and overall system resilience.

  • Platform Integrations: Lead the design and implementation of integrations with internal and external platforms to expand advertising targeting, measurement, and data capabilities.

  • Global Collaboration: Work closely with engineering teams in the US and India to drive successful project execution, share technical knowledge, and ensure alignment across distributed teams.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 10+ years of professional software engineering experience building and operating large-scale, production-grade software systems.

  • Demonstrated experience leading the architecture and delivery of complex, distributed systems with significant scale, throughput, reliability, or data processing requirements.

  • Strong proficiency in one or more programming languages, such as Go, Scala, Python, Java, or C++, along with a deep understanding of computer science fundamentals.

  • Extensive experience with distributed systems, concurrency, data structures, algorithms, system design, and performance optimization.

  • Hands-on experience with big data technologies such as Apache Spark and Databricks, and data storage and caching technologies such as MySQL, Redis, or ElastiCache.

  • Experience designing, deploying, and operating cloud-native systems using AWS, Kubernetes, and related infrastructure technologies.

  • Ability to navigate, understand, and refactor large, complex codebases while maintaining high standards of reliability and maintainability.

  • Strong understanding of system observability, production troubleshooting, fault tolerance, capacity planning, and cost optimization.

  • Proven ability to make sound architectural trade-offs, evaluate alternative approaches, and influence technical decisions across multiple teams.

  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to diverse stakeholders.

  • Demonstrated ability to mentor engineers, guide technical discussions, and raise engineering standards across teams.

  • Experience collaborating with globally distributed engineering teams and driving projects across geographical boundaries.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building and scaling ad tech platforms, including ad serving, audience targeting, advertising measurement, or real-time bidding systems.

  • Proven track record of leading multi-team technical initiatives and delivering significant business and engineering outcomes.

  • Experience designing high-throughput, low-latency services and large-scale data processing pipelines.

  • Experience with cloud cost optimization, distributed resource management, and large-scale infrastructure efficiency.

  • Experience defining architecture standards, technical roadmaps, and engineering practices across teams.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence without direct authority and drive alignment across engineering, product, and operations.

  • Experience mentoring senior engineers and developing technical leaders.

  • Experience working in a global engineering organization with teams across India and the US.

title: CAE/PLM Senior Principal Software Architect (Design)

This role serves as a functional technical advisor, applying deep expertise in desktop application architecture, interactive 3D systems, and computational engineering software to address emerging technical challenges and drive innovation with broad business impact.

The Senior Principal Software Architect establishes and executes architectural strategies, leads major technical initiatives, and influences the development of scalable application frameworks and GPU-enabled computational infrastructure. Working across DES, Platform, and related engineering functions, this individual ensures architectural consistency, reduces systemic technical risk, and enables multiple teams to deliver high-quality engineering software at scale.

  • Establish shared application frameworks, architecture standards, and reusable software capabilities that support development across the DES organization.
  • Lead the architecture of scalable GPU compute orchestration, clustered GPU job scheduling, and resource management for computationally intensive engineering workflows.

  • E08 / Sr. Principal Engineer: $197,990 - $272,240

$171,450—$314,390 USD

title: Home Visitor
description:
POSITION SUMMARY: Responsible for the delivery of comprehensive home based services to children and families. Will establish positive, supportive and reciprocal relationships with families and children to promote children’s progress as described in the Head Start Early Learning Outcomes Framework.

Schedule: Monday - Friday 7:30am - 4:00pm

Please apply online at

Only completed and signed applications will be considered.

Full Time Position- Benefits Eligible: Teacher Break Pay, Sick, PTO, Employer paid health benefits, Vision & Dental Plans, 403B retirement, company paid holidays, Pet Insurance, Employer Paid Basic $30,000 Life Insurance Policy, Employer Paid Long-Term Disability Insurance (LTD) and Employer Paid Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance (AD&D). Public Service Loan Forgiveness Qualified Employer.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

  • Coordinate bi-monthly socializations that include experiences and opportunities for parents that allow infants and toddlers to maximize their growth and development across all domains.
  • Coordinate experiences and opportunities during planned weekly home visits (90 minutes each) with the parent that allow infants and toddlers to maximize their growth and development across all domains by implementing an individualized plan based on both formal and informal assessments.
  • Assist families in understanding child development and identification of developmentally appropriate expectations.
  • Schedule, support, and follow through with developmental screenings of infants and toddlers in collaboration with their family.
  • Support and encourage parent-child bonding, attachment, and parent’s development of relationship-based, responsive caregiving.
  • Promote the primary goal of supporting child/parent interactions and relationships during socializations. Encourage families to network and socialize.
  • Support families in providing an appropriate environment and activities which support their child’s education, intellectual, social-emotional, motor, and language abilities.
  • Provide parents with guidance on home safety, nutrition, effective discipline, constructive play activities, and other related topics.
  • Encourage parent involvement and parent participation according to program guidelines.
  • Maintain confidentiality and accurate records on each child’s progress, all aspects of client, staff, and agency information.
  • Develop and implement a weekly lesson plan and provide an organized program according to the identified curriculum.
  • Maintain child records and inventory of equipment and materials.
  • Develop an ongoing weekly individualization plan for each child based on needs and strengths identified through screening, assessment, and input from specialists and parents.
  • Maintain updated observations and anecdotal notes to document each child’s progress in identified assessment system.
  • Complete and submit all attendance, lesson plans, assessments, reports and other data required in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Communicate regularly with Learning and Development Manager (LDM) regarding any changes in home visit activities, child’s status, work schedule, supply and equipment needs or other issues or concerns.
  • Work with other staff and team members to refer children and families for additional services.
  • Serve as a liaison for, and provide support to program staff in communication with parents and implementation of parent related functions.
  • Assist in, and provide for the seamless transition of children entering and/or exiting the Home Base program.
  • Maintain effective working interaction with peers, subordinates and outside contacts that will enhance the operation of the HS/EHS program.
  • Act as an advocate and role model for HS/EHS families. Recruit children for the program.
  • Attend and actively participate in training programs, staff meetings, and other meeting/trainings.
  • Participate in community activities that enhance Head Start programs as directed.
  • Participate in ongoing monitoring, Community Assessment and Self-Assessment and performs reasonable related functions.
  • Participate in regular safety, storm and fire drills.
  • Use and follow the policies/procedures of Head Start, federal, state and local regulations/laws, and federal regulations/laws including the Head Start Performance Standards, applicable transmittal notices, and other administrative orders/directions.
  • Use and follow the policies/procedures of You Thrive Florida, including but not limited to Personnel Policies, Occupational Health and Safety policies, payroll policies/practices, etc.

NON-ESSENTIAL/SECONDARY FUNCTIONS:

Perform any additional duties as directed or assigned by supervisor, management staff, program director or You Thrive Florida management staff. This description is intended to convey information essential to understanding the scope of the position and is not intended to be an exhaustive list of skills, efforts, duties, responsibilities, or working conditions associated with the position.

title: MCAI Software Engineer
description:
Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.


Department OverviewWe build and maintain high-quality voice and data communication systems for mission-critical operations and public safety. Working in small, autonomous teams and collaborating across our global offices, we focus on engineering dependable infrastructure where uptime and low latency are vital.
Job Description

The Role

Our users rely heavily on our tools daily, and their feedback loop is tight and demanding. If you have experience shipping production software and want to actively shape our development standards rather than just maintain legacy workflows, this role gives you the space to do it.

To support the ongoing growth of our platforms, we are seeking software engineers to build AI-driven solutions that seamlessly connect with our core communication services. You will contribute across the full lifecycle: designing, building, testing, deploying, and maintaining software. Success in this role requires strong technical craft paired with a genuine commitment to understanding customer workflows. Together, we engineer systems built for high performance, precision, and dependability.

Our Development Culture

  • Dedicated R&D Time: We reserve 10% of your working time for exploratory side projects, tooling improvements, and continuous learning.
  • Modern Developer Tooling: We dogfood our AI systems internally and equip the team with modern AI tooling to accelerate delivery while keeping code quality high.
  • High Autonomy, Small Teams: Engineers own their systems end-to-end and have a direct say in architecture, tech choices, and roadmap priorities.
  • Blameless & Collaborative: We treat mistakes as learning opportunities through blameless post-mortems and prioritize knowledge sharing over gatekeeping.
  • Empathetic Code Reviews: We believe high engineering standards and kind, constructive communication go hand in hand.

Tech Stack

Elixir, TypeScript, Angular, Kubernetes, Docker, Azure, Redis, NATS.io, Azure DevOps, GitHub, Helm.


Basic Requirements

What We’re Looking For

  • A degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical production experience.
  • Experience with functional programming. Ideally in Elixir, Erlang, or similar, though we are happy to cross-train engineers with a strong interest in functional design.
  • Solid understanding of core software engineering practices: automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, and clean architecture.
  • Experience with (or strong technical interest in) distributed systems, microservices, and high-availability/low-latency services.
  • Clear, proactive communication in English.
  • A willingness to mentor peers, review code thoughtfully, and receive feedback with an open mind.

Nice to Have

  • Hands-on experience containerizing and orchestrating services using Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Familiarity with high-throughput message brokers (NATS.io, Kafka, RabbitMQ) and efficient serialization/RPC protocols (Protocol Buffers, gRPC).
  • Practical exposure to cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, or GCP).
  • Experience building or consuming modern AI/LLM APIs and toolchains in production.

Bring your passion, potential, and talents to Motorola Solutions, and help us usher in a new era in public safety and security.

Relocation ProvidedNone

title: Senior Instructional Designer & Learning Consultant
location: OK Oklahoma City - Oklahoma City, OK 73129
description:
United Petroleum Transports | Florida Rock & Tank Lines

Senior Instructional Designer & Learning Consultant

Location: Corporate Office – 100% On-Site – Downtown - Oklahoma City, OK

Department: Organizational Development

Reports To: Senior Manager of Organizational Development

Salary: $65,000–$85,000 annually, based on experience

Travel: Up to 25%

FLSA: Exempt

Before You Build Anything, You Want to Understand the Problem

Do you enjoy taking a vague and incomplete training request, digging into what is really going on, and determining the solution that will actually work?

A request comes in. The details are thin and the real problem is not obvious yet. Some people wait to be told what to do step by step to build. You start moving—figuring out who to talk to, what to ask, what to observe, and what the work actually requires. Then you own it from there!

If that sounds like you, keep reading.

UPT and FRTL are building our Organizational Development function from the ground up, and we need a senior instructional designer who can proactively step in, think independently, consult across the organization, and own the work from the first conversation to the results. Most days you will not receive a polished brief. You will receive a document, a system update, or a request that says, "We need training on this." Your job is to figure out what is actually needed. We can teach you our business, systems, and culture. You bring the instructional design expertise.

What this role is: a senior-level, consultative instructional design role. You own the whole project: figuring out what is really needed, recommending the solution, building it well, and knowing whether it worked.

What this role is not: an order-taking or content-creator role. If your instinct is to take what you are handed and make it look polished in Rise, this is not the right fit. It is also not an administrative, training coordination, graphic design, teacher or technical writing role.

The Work

You will be handed a problem, not a plan.

A request comes from a leader, a safety concern, an operational change, or a new system. It may arrive as a document, a messy deck, a hallway conversation, or one sentence in an email. What happens next is yours to determine. Nobody here will hand you a scope, a task list, or a set of next steps—that is the expertise you bring.

You are accountable for:

  • Owning projects end to end across safety, compliance, operations, onboarding, leadership development, and enterprise initiatives—from the first conversation through what happens after launch.
  • Consulting across the organization. Much of what you need is not written down. It lives with drivers, technicians, dispatchers, supervisors, and leaders, and you are the one who goes and gets it.
  • Identifying the real problem and recommending the right solution—including when that solution is not training—and being able to explain what led you there.
  • Deciding what gets built, in what modality, and why: eLearning, video, instructor-led, blended, job aids, facilitator materials, performance support, or practice. You match the solution to the audience and the work, not to your favorite tool.
  • Producing accurate, accessible, professional work along with everything that surrounds it, then getting it into people's hands and making sure it lands.
  • Proving whether it worked, in terms the business recognizes, and going back to improve it.
  • Researching—what already exists internally, what good looks like elsewhere, and where AI makes you faster without making the work generic.
  • Managing multiple projects, stakeholders, and timelines at once, and keeping people informed without being asked in a fast-paced environment.
  • Helping build the standards, templates, and practices of a growing OD function.

How You Think Matters

  • You lead with curiosity. "I don't know" is not an answer—it tells you what to research, who to observe, and who to talk to next.
  • You can hear a stakeholder say, "I need training" and still hear the business problem underneath. You know the difference between what someone asks for and what analysis shows they need.
  • You operate well when the path is not fully defined, and you bring innovation, ideas that elevate the request rather than reproducing what was handed to you – add value!
  • You challenge assumptions respectfully, consult comfortably at every level from frontline to senior leadership, and when you make a recommendation, you can explain why.
  • You have a repeatable way of working through a project, and you know when to adapt to it. A process guides your thinking—it does not replace it.

title: Senior GTM Program Manager
description:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

The Go To Market (GTM) Performance & Strategy team turns company and go-to-market strategy into coordinated execution and measurable performance. In this role, you’ll lead complex, cross-functional programs across strategic priorities such as market expansion, New Product Introduction (NPI), acquisitions, and GTM transformation while building scalable ways of working. Your work will help 1Password advance its mission to enable people and organizations to work securely and productively.

How we’re using AI today

Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.

Expectations of this role

This is a hybrid ole. You will be expected to work from 1Password's Toronto or Austin office 3 days per week, with the flexibility to work from the office up to 5 days based on business needs.

Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto.

What we're looking for:

  • Bring 6+ years of experience in strategic program management, business operations, GTM strategy and operations, transformation, management consulting, or a related role within a technology or Software as a Service (SaaS) organization.

  • Demonstrate experience working in a channel-led or channel-centric go-to-market environment.

  • Lead complex, cross-functional programs involving senior executives, multiple teams, ambiguity, and competing priorities.

  • Apply NPI experience to help teams move from planning through launch and execution.

  • Facilitate senior-level discussions, challenge assumptions constructively, surface difficult topics, and drive clear decisions.

  • Build practical operating mechanisms that create accountability, visibility, and momentum without adding unnecessary process.

  • Use artificial intelligence (AI), automation, and modern program-management tools to streamline workflows, synthesize information, and improve execution quality.

What you can expect:

  • Lead high-impact cross-functional programs from definition through execution across GTM and company priorities.

  • Translate ambiguous objectives into clear outcomes, workstreams, owners, milestones, dependencies, risks, decision points, and success measures.

  • Drive alignment and accountability across Sales, Customer Experience, Marketing, Product Marketing, Product Management, Revenue Operations, People, Corporate Strategy & Operations, and other teams.

  • Represent GTM in formal NPI stage-gate processes and help coordinate launches across stakeholders.

  • Build operating rhythms and program frameworks that provide visibility into priorities, progress, dependencies, decisions, risks, and outcomes.

  • Manage GTM operating capabilities, including knowledge and content governance, by establishing ownership, review standards, and processes for resolving outdated or conflicting information.

  • Create concise, executive-ready program updates that surface risks, tradeoffs, recommendations, and decisions requiring leadership attention.

USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $162,000 USD and $235,000 USD.. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $155,000 CAD and $225,000 CAD. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.


Our culture
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results.

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.


Our approach to work
We recognize the power of both in person collaboration and remote work. Some roles are designated as remote-first, with an expectation that individuals work from their homes majority of the time, while others are designated as in-office roles, with an expectation of being on-site on a regular basis. We recognize that certain roles benefit from regular, in-person connection to support collaboration, team cohesion, and customer engagement.

For all roles, occasional travel may be required. This includes things like: department-wide offsites, quarterly department meetings and periodic customer events. These events are typically held in varying locations across Canada, USA and/or EMEA. In leadership roles, you can expect to travel once per month on average.

Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto.


What we offer
We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer:

🩺 Competitive health benefits
🏝 Generous PTO policy

Growth and future

Community

🏆 Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly
🌎 Remote-first work environment
*Some roles in our GTM team are currently being hired for in-person hybrid work in Toronto and Austin. These roles will specify on the posting.

You belong here.

1Password is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. title: Software Engineer, Privacy & Data Governance
description:
About Thinking Machines

The mission of Thinking Machines is to build AI that extends human will and judgment. We are training frontier models with Inkling, developing Tinker to let people make models their own, and crafting interfaces that broaden human-AI communication. We believe the future worth building is human, and we're hiring people who want to build it.

About the Role

We're looking for an engineer to help manage how data is handled across Thinking Machines: what we collect and acquire, where it is stored, who and what systems can access it, how long we keep it, and how it's used in training, evaluation, and products. You'll help build the systems that let us protect privacy and make definitive statements about our practices from data inventory and classification through access and purpose controls to retention, deletion, and audit. You'll also collaborate closely with researchers and product engineers to answer privacy questions that don’t have textbook answers.

This is a role for someone who knows privacy deeply and treats it as an engineering problem rather than a checklist. The questions we face are rarely settled by policy alone: what it means to honor a deletion request against a trained model; how customers' fine-tuning data on Tinker should be isolated, never commingled, and only used for the customer; when to deidentify data (and how) vs. apply differential privacy to it. We want someone who can weigh privacy against model quality, research velocity, and product usefulness, pick a defensible answer, and then build it.

What You'll Do

  • Implement and enforce privacy and data governance across internal systems day to day by building systems like data classification tagging, retention jobs, deletion pipelines, and data classifiers and integrating them across systems at Thinking Machines.

  • Build the isolation guarantees that keep customer and user data separate and protected, including the training data customers bring to Tinker and the conversations people have with our interfaces.

  • Run privacy reviews and threat models on new data sources, training runs, and product features, and close them out by shipping the control, the check, or the tooling, not only a recommendation.

  • Translate legal and policy requirements (GDPR, CCPA, contractual commitments) into working code: policy-as-code, CI checks, and pipeline enforcement, built and maintained by you.

  • Maintain shared libraries and guardrails that make the private path the default, and fix them when they break or fall out of date.

Skills and Qualifications

Minimum qualifications

  • Built and shipped at least one production privacy or data governance system (retention/deletion pipeline, policy evaluation engine, data cataloging and/or lineage system, consent system, or similar) and owned it through to operation, not just design.

  • Written and operated production code in Python or a comparable language, evidenced by a system you can walk through in detail: what it does, how it fails, how you debugged it.

  • Direct experience with enforcing privacy or governing data in an AI/ML data pipeline (training data, fine-tuning, inference, or evaluation) and can describe a specific privacy risk you identified or mitigated in one of these systems.

  • Has chosen pragmatic controls over ideal ones on real systems, and can describe what was shipped as a result.

  • Has written a technical requirement or control directly from a legal or policy obligation (GDPR, CCPA, or similar), and can name the obligation and the control.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience at an AI lab or with ML infrastructure: training data curation, multi-tenant fine-tuning platforms, or inference systems that handle user data.

  • Has implemented a privacy-enhancing technique (deidentification, differential privacy, secure enclaves) in a real system, and can describe where it fell short.

  • Experience building data lineage, metadata, or policy-engine tooling, or large-scale deletion and retention systems.

  • Background in security engineering, or has worked directly with a security team on access control implementation.

  • Has been one of the first engineers building out a privacy function, and can point to the specific systems they personally built, not just the program they ran.

Logistics

  • Location: This role is based in San Francisco, California.

  • Compensation: Depending on background, skills and experience, the expected annual salary range for this position is $300,000 - $350,000 USD.

  • Visa sponsorship: We sponsor visas. While we can't guarantee success for every candidate or role, if you're the right fit, we're committed to working through the visa process together.

  • Benefits: Thinking Machines offers generous health, dental, and vision benefits, unlimited PTO, paid parental leave, and relocation support as needed.

title: Customer Experience Test Automation Intern
description:
🎨 OpusClip is the world's No.1 AI video agent, built for authenticity on social media.

We envision a world where everyone can authentically share their story through video, with no expertise needed. Within just 18 months of our launch, over 20 million creators and businesses have used OpusClip to enhance their social presence.

We have raised $50 million in total funding and are fortunate to have some of the most supportive investors, including SoftBank Vision Fund, DCM Ventures, Millennium New Horizons, Fellows Fund, AI Grant, Jason Lemkin (SaaStr), Samsung Next, GTMfund, Alumni Ventures, and many more.

Check out our latest coverage by Business Insider featuring our product and funding milestones, and our recognition as one of The Information's 50 Most Promising Startups in 2024.

Headquartered in Mountain View, we are a team of 100 passionate and experienced AI enthusiasts and video experts, driven by our core values:

  • Be a Champion Team

  • Prioritize Ruthlessly

  • Ship fast, Quality Follows

  • Obsess over customers

Be a part of this exciting journey with us!

About the Role

OpusClip is hiring a CX Test Automation Intern: a software-developer-in-test who sits inside the Customer Experience team and turns real customer tickets into automated UI end-to-end tests. You will be the first person in a new lane we call customer-originated requirements: the thousands of support conversations we handle each month are a rich record of how OpusClip actually gets used and where it breaks, and nobody has yet turned that record into a repeatable test battery.

This is a 4-month co-op based in Vancouver, starting January 7, 2027, with the option to extend for a further 8 months. The first 4 months hold a bounded, well-defined backlog that is valuable on its own; the extension is a decision we make together, not an assumption.

You will work with AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex) every day, ship real automation into a real product, and leave with a portfolio of tests that protect paying customers. CX at OpusClip is built as a talent nursery: people who start here move into data, engineering and customer-facing technical roles. This role is designed as one of those on-ramps.

This role suits a student or early-career engineer who has already built and shipped something with AI assistance, likes finding the edge cases others miss, and cares about the people on the other side of the product as much as the code.

Key Responsibilities

Turn customer tickets into automated tests

Your core output is a UI end-to-end test battery grounded in real customer reports. You will mine support conversations and bug tickets for the workflows customers actually run and the moments where they fail, reproduce those failures, and write automated tests that catch them before the next customer does. Each test traces back to a ticket, so the battery grows in the direction of real user pain rather than hypothetical coverage. Success here is measured by the share of customer-reported regressions your tests would have caught, and by how much faster CX can confirm a reported issue is real.

Map user workflows into testable moments

Before a test exists, someone has to break a workflow like "upload a video, get clips, export to TikTok" into its discrete steps, decision points and failure modes, and rank them by how many customers they touch. You will do this mapping with the CX team, who hold the ticket data, and document it so that Product and Engineering can reuse it. Over time this becomes a living map of how OpusClip is used, maintained from the customer side.

Work AI-native

You will build with Claude Code or Codex as your primary tool: scoping a task, giving the model the right context, breaking the work into steps, reviewing and iterating on the output, and knowing when the first answer is wrong. You will also help the CX team adopt the same habits, sharing patterns and small tools that let non-engineers verify issues and query data on their own.

Bridge CX and Engineering

You sit in CX but your work lands in Engineering's repositories and CI. You will open pull requests, respond to code review, follow branch and merge conventions, and report flaky or failing tests with clear reproduction steps. When a test exposes a product gap, you will write it up with the customer context, the business impact and a proposed priority, so that the people who own the fix can act on it without a second round of questions.

Qualifications and Requirements

Hands-on vibe coding experience: Must-have. You have built and shipped something real with AI assistance (a side project, internal tool or script) and can walk through how it was built: what you asked for, what the model got wrong, and how you fixed it.

Can read Python and JavaScript/TypeScript: Must-have. You can explain what a short snippet does and spot an obvious bug. You do not need to write either language from scratch.

Testing mindset: Must-have. Given a feature such as "upload a video, get clips", you list the happy path, edge cases and failure modes, then rank them by user impact rather than by how easy they are to test.

Customer empathy: Must-have. You want to understand what the user was trying to do, not just what broke. You read a ticket and see a person with a deadline, not a bug ID.

Clear communication and cross-functional collaboration: Must-have. Your write-ups are short, specific and readable by someone who was not in the room. You ask for review and take feedback without friction.

Grasp of business impact: Must-have. You can reason about ROI and opportunity cost: why fixing a bug that hits 2% of paying exports beats one that hits a rarely used free feature, and what it costs to test the wrong thing.

Breaks user workflows into discrete moments: Must-have. You can take "upload a video, get clips, post to TikTok" and name each step, each decision the user makes and each place it can go wrong.

Curiosity or background in video editing and media: Nice-to-have. You have made, edited or published video, or follow creators closely enough to know what a good clip looks like and why someone would pay for one.

Proficient with Claude Code or Codex: Nice-to-have. You give the tool the right context, break a task into steps and iterate on the output rather than accepting the first answer.

Basic web tooling and Git: Nice-to-have. You are comfortable in browser DevTools (Network and Console tabs, element selectors) and with branches, commits and pull requests, including taking review feedback.

What We Offer

You will own a real test battery that protects paying customers, with your name on every pull request. You will work with AI coding tools as a daily practice, not a demo, and build a track record that is unusual for an intern: automated tests traced to customer evidence, shipped into a production product.

You will have direct access to the CX, Product and Engineering teams at a fast-growing AI video company, and a manager whose explicit goal is to move strong CX people into technical roles across the company.

How to Apply

Send a link to something you built with AI assistance (GitHub, a deployed app, a script, an internal tool) and two or three sentences on what it does and what the model got wrong along the way. A resume is helpful but the project matters more.

EEO

OpusClip is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. OpusClip considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Opus Clip is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures.

title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
At Didero, we’re building the autonomous supply chain, starting with agentic supplier management.

Global trade has never been more complex or more critical. Teams are underwater, reacting to a flood of challenges — from geopolitical risk to tariffs. Didero helps by automating time-intensive workflows with AI agents, deploying cutting-edge technology into one of the world’s most vital domains.

We’re backed by some of the world’s best venture funds and leading figures across AI, supply chain, and enterprise software.

About the Role

We are looking for a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer to join our team. This role is ideal for a technically strong, customer-facing engineer who can understand complex customer operations, question requirements, design scalable solutions, and build the systems needed to deploy Didero successfully.

You will work directly with our enterprise and strategic customers to understand their end-to-end procurement and operations workflows including ERP integrations, data pipelines, workflow automation, supplier communication flows, reporting, and custom deployment needs. You will translate messy real-world processes into reliable, maintainable technical systems.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You will build backend systems, integrations, APIs, data pipelines, and workflow automations using the best technical approach for the problem. While our core platform is built with Django, we care more about solving customer problems than using any single technology. You'll use the right tools and technologies for each integration or deployment.

You will work with systems such as NetSuite, SAP, Microsoft Business Central, Zip, and other procurement, ERP, finance, and operational platforms. You will also partner closely with Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and Forward Deployed teams to ensure customer deployments are scalable and aligned with our product direction.

We are looking for someone who is not just an implementer. The right person is a systems thinker who asks why, challenges assumptions, pushes back on unclear requirements, and helps customers arrive at better solutions.

Please Note: This is a hybrid role based in NYC and may involve occasional on-site work with customers, approximately 1-2 per month, to support discovery sessions, technical workshops, and deployment phases.

What You’ll Do

  • Work directly with customers to understand their procurement, finance, ERP, and operational workflows.

  • Question and clarify customer requirements, identifying the underlying business need rather than blindly implementing requests.

  • Design and build integrations with ERP, procurement, finance, and operational systems.

  • Build backend services, APIs, data pipelines, workflow automations, and customer-specific technical solutions.

  • Translate ambiguous customer processes into structured, scalable system designs.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to identify repeatable patterns that should become part of the core platform.

  • Debug complex integration issues across customer systems, third-party APIs, data models, and internal services.

  • Support customer discovery, deployment planning, and technical implementation.

  • Help define best practices for forward-deployed engineering, customer pipelines, and integration architecture.

You’ll be successful in this role if you…

  • Thrive in ambiguity and make steady progress without perfectly defined requirements.

  • Think in systems, connecting customer workflows, data, and software into scalable solutions.

  • Partner directly with customers to uncover root problems rather than simply implementing requests.

  • Challenge assumptions and refine requirements before writing code.

  • Exercise strong engineering judgment, knowing when to build custom solutions, create reusable abstractions, or push back.

  • Balance customer-specific needs with long-term product thinking by identifying repeatable patterns.

  • Debug complex integration and distributed systems problems methodically.

  • Communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders alike.

Qualifications

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience with strong backend expertise.

  • Strong experience building backend services using Python and/or Django (or comparable backend technologies).

  • Experience designing and building integrations with external systems, APIs, enterprise software, or data pipelines.

  • Experience working directly with customers or cross-functional stakeholders to translate business requirements into technical solutions.

  • Strong understanding of distributed systems, API design, debugging, and systems architecture.

  • Excellent communication and problem-solving skills.

Bonus Points For:

  • Experience working in Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Engineering, or Implementation Engineering.

  • Prior experience integrating multiple ERP systems.

  • Familiarity with SAP OData services, NetSuite SuiteTalk/SuiteScript, Microsoft Business Central APIs.

  • Experience with async processing (Celery, Redis, RabbitMQ) for large data sync jobs.

  • Familiarity with Docker, cloud deployment (AWS/Azure/GCP).

  • Knowledge of financial/accounting workflows and supply chain processes.

Tech Stack

Django · Python · React · TypeScript

What we value at Didero

  • We go beyond OTIF. We’re obsessed with our customers and go above and beyond to ensure we’re their top supplier. We work hard to earn and maintain their trust.

  • Own it. We own what we do. We stand behind the quality of our work and do the right thing, especially when it costs us.

  • Move fast. Learn faster. We have a strong bias to action and shorten the cycle by following our curiosity to improve as we go.

  • Be relentless. When one route closes, we find another.

  • Disagree, then commit. This is an open contest of ideas. We’re direct, but with respect. We’re decisive, and everyone commits because we win together.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive compensation and equity

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Memberships for One Medical, Talkspace, Teladoc, and Kindbody

  • Unlimited PTO — we trust you to take the time you need

  • Monthly wellness stipend via ClassPass

  • Tech equipment for your setup

  • Catered lunches (for those in the office)

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Senior Software Engineer (Full-Stack, AI-Native)

Marvin · Denver/Los Angeles - Hybrid 2-day in office · Full-time · $160k-190k

About Marvin

Marvin helps people navigate their mental health and wellbeing. We partner with employers and health plans to give their members one place to understand their coverage, find care, and get support, including an AI coach built into the product. We're a small team shipping a production healthcare application, which means every engineer touches things that matter and owns them end to end.

The role

We're hiring a senior full-stack engineer who has made AI a core part of how they build software, not a novelty. This is not a machine learning research role. You won't train models or tune GPUs. You will ship product in a modern TypeScript/Next.js stack, and you'll do it with AI woven into both the product and your own workflow.

Two things distinguish this role from a standard senior web position:

  1. You build with AI. You've moved well past autocomplete. You direct agentic coding tools to do real, multi-step work, you know exactly where they break, and you own every line they produce.

  2. You build AI into the product. You've shipped LLM-backed features to real users and lived with them in production: prompts, tool calls, evals, tracing, cost, latency, and failure modes.

What you'll do

  • Own features end to end across our Next.js/React/TypeScript app, Prisma/Postgres backend, and AWS infrastructure.

  • Extend our AI coach and build new LLM-powered member experiences: retrieval over benefits data, structured extraction, guided flows, and agentic tool use against our own APIs.

  • Design evaluation and observability for AI features so we know when they get worse, not just when they crash.

  • Push our AI-assisted development practice forward: agent instructions, reusable skills, hooks, MCP integrations, and review practices that keep quality high as velocity climbs.

  • Handle sensitive health data responsibly. PHI boundaries, redaction, audit trails, and vendor data agreements are part of the design, not an afterthought.

  • Review code, whether written by a human or an agent, with a critical eye. Mentor teammates and raise the bar on testing and reliability.

What we're looking for

Core engineering

  • 5+ years building production web applications, with deep TypeScript, React, and Node experience. Next.js is a strong plus.

  • Comfort across the stack: relational data modeling (we use Prisma and Postgres), auth flows, caching, background jobs, and cloud deployment (AWS, Docker, Terraform or similar).

  • A real testing habit at every layer: unit, component, and end-to-end. We use Vitest, Storybook, Cypress, and Playwright.

  • Strong product judgment and the ability to work directly with design, clinical, and partner-facing teammates.

AI fluency (the part that sets you apart)

  • Daily, expert use of agentic coding tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex. You write project instructions and reusable skills for your agents, hand them multi-step tasks, and review the output like a senior reviewer, not a rubber stamp.

  • Hands-on experience shipping LLM features: prompt design and versioning, structured outputs, tool/function calling, streaming UIs, retrieval-augmented generation, and multi-turn conversation state.

  • You've run evals and traced production LLM traffic (LangSmith, Braintrust, Langfuse, or homegrown), and you can explain what changed the last time a model version bumped underneath you.

  • You understand the cost, latency, and quality triangle and have made real trade-offs: model selection, caching, prompt compression, and fallback strategies.

  • Clear-eyed about limits. You know when an LLM is the wrong tool, how to constrain one when it's the right tool, and how to keep a hallucination from ever reaching a member.

Nice to have

  • Healthcare, benefits, or other regulated-data experience (HIPAA, SOC 2).

  • Building MCP servers or internal agent tooling for a team.

  • Experience with Clerk, Stripe, or Sentry.

  • Contributions to AI developer tooling, open source or internal.

How we work

AI is part of our engineering culture, not a side experiment. Our repository ships with agent configuration, we maintain shared skills for code review and security checks, and we expect engineers to spend more of their time on judgment and less on typing. We also expect the opposite discipline: no unreviewed AI-generated code lands, and "the agent wrote it" is never an explanation for a bug.

Compensation and benefits

160-190k base salary · Equity · Health, dental, and vision · [401(k)] · Unlimited PTO · Hybrid 2 days/wk in office (LA or Denver)

The Inflight Policy & Procedure Specialist is responsible for developing solutions related to policies and procedures applicable to inflight functions at Alaska Airlines.
