description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

  • As a Sustainability Program Manager, you will be an important member of Crusoe's sustainability team, transforming sustainability commitments into day-to-day operational reality. You will own the processes, training, and tracking that make our sustainability KPIs achievable and enforceable across a rapidly expanding portfolio of AI data centers and energy assets. You’ll work directly with cross-functional teams to translate targets into requirements, workflows, and accountability at the site and project level. This role suits someone with technical fluency in how manufacturing facilities and data centers are built and run, who is energized by designing scalable processes, driving adoption, and closing the gap between commitment and performance.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Lead operational sustainability initiatives related to water, waste, and carbon, from scoping through delivery, building project plans, aligning stakeholders, tracking milestones, and surfacing risks early.

  • Support sustainability implementation throughout the lifecycle of data center projects by helping to define, monitor, and improve data center construction and operational efficiency metrics, including embodied carbon, waste diversion, PUE, and WUE. Partner with internal teams and external partners to identify performance gaps and drive improvements.

  • Design and implement the processes, SOPs, and checklists that embed sustainability requirements into manufacturing, construction, commissioning, and site operations, and train site teams, contractors, and partners to apply them consistently.

  • Support green building certification strategies (e.g., LEED, Green Globes) across new builds, coordinating documentation, consultants, and design team inputs.

  • Build and maintain dashboards, trackers, and automated workflows that give teams timely visibility into operational performance, using AI-enabled tools to reduce manual effort.

  • Manage renewable energy tracking and energy performance data, working with Energy, Finance, and Operations teams to monitor portfolio status and surface risks and opportunities.

  • Provide as-needed support across the broader sustainability team, flexing into emerging priorities, ad-hoc data requests, and new initiatives as the business evolves.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in engineering, environmental science, sustainability, data analytics, or a related field. Candidates from other backgrounds with demonstrated technical depth are encouraged to apply.

  • Experience: 4-7 years of professional experience in sustainability operations, construction or energy management, supply chain or supplier management, or environmental consulting, ideally within the data center, cloud infrastructure, energy, or technology sectors. This should include hands-on management of operational programs, performance metrics, or compliance and enforcement processes.

  • Data Center & Energy Knowledge: Strong understanding of data center construction and operations, including metrics (PUE, WUE, CUE) and power, cooling, and energy systems. Familiarity with renewable energy instruments and energy markets.

  • Program Leadership: Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, manage competing priorities, and influence stakeholders.

  • Process Design: Proven ability to design, document, and roll out scalable processes, SOPs, and controls across many stakeholders and sites, and to drive adoption and adherence.

  • Supply Chain & Vendor Engagement: Experience engaging suppliers, contractors, or vendors to set requirements, build capability, and hold them accountable to performance expectations, including through contract terms, scorecards, and corrective action.

  • Technical & Analytical Skills: Advanced proficiency in Excel and strong data skills, such as SQL, Python, or BI tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, Looker). Experience building trackers, dashboards, and data quality controls.

  • Communication & Collaboration: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex sustainability data into clear narratives for diverse stakeholders.

  • Adaptability & Ownership: Self-starter who exercises sound judgment under ambiguity, proactively surfaces risks and opportunities, and takes full ownership of outcomes in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

Bonus Points:

  • Familiarity with green building certifications (LEED AP, Green Globes) or embodied carbon in construction, including whole building LCA tools (e.g., EC3, One Click LCA, Tally).

  • Experience running supplier engagement or responsible sourcing programs, such as supplier scorecards, audits, or sustainability requirements in procurement.

  • Comfort using AI tools (e.g., Claude, Gemini) to build trackers, automate workflows, or improve efficiency.

  • Experience with construction project management, contractor compliance programs, or EHS/quality management systems.

Benefits:

  • Health insurance package options that include HDHP and PPO, vision, and dental for you and your dependents

  • Employer contributions to HSA accounts

  • Generous paid time off and holiday schedule

Compensation will be paid in the range of $130,000 - $160,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

4. Final Stage Interview (if applicable)

What to expect from our hiring process

Our process is designed to be fair, transparent and straightforward. Stages vary depending on the role — more senior positions may involve additional steps, and some areas include role-specific assessments such as a technical test or case study — but typically you can expect:

title: Lead Software Engineer
description:
ROLE SUMMARY

Are you a hands-on engineer who raises the bar for everyone around you?


Join us at FTSE Russell in London. We’re establishing a team of engineers passionate about software craftsmanship, quality, and meaningful impact. As a Lead Software Engineer, you’ll own the technical direction of software that powers the indices trusted by financial institutions worldwide.


We build primarily in Python, so that’s our preference — but depth of engineering judgement matters more to us than the language on your CV. If you’ve led the design and delivery of serious production systems in Java, C#, C, C++, Scala, Go, or Rust and you’re motivated to lead in Python, we’d like to talk. At this level, we expect you to become fluent quickly and bring that cross-language engineering perspective with you.


This is a hands-on Lead Individual Contributor role — not a people management role. You’ll still be designing, writing, and reviewing code every week. What changes at this level is scope: you’ll own architecture and technical direction in a defined area, mentor and grow the engineers around you, and raise engineering quality across the team through good design, reuse, strong standards, and hands-on support.


The systems we build handle significant volumes of financial data and support products used across global financial markets. There is real depth in the data and distributed systems challenges — but you’re being hired first and foremost as a software engineer who leads through technical judgement and code.


If you’re excited about building systems that matter, solving difficult engineering problems, and making the engineers around you better, we’d love to meet you.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

We’re building the next-generation index data platform at FTSE Russell — and we want you to shape it with us:

  • Staying hands-on — designing, writing, reviewing, and shipping production software, primarily in Python, and setting the standard for what good engineering looks like through the code you deliver
  • Owning technical direction and architecture for a defined area of the platform, making trade-offs explicit so the team can move quickly and confidently
  • Leading the design of software systems — services, APIs, shared libraries, and the interfaces between them — with resilience, performance, maintainability, and reusability designed in
  • Driving engineering quality across the team: raising the bar in code review, reducing duplication through well-designed shared components, and championing testing, refactoring, automation, and secure development practices
  • Mentoring and coaching engineers through pairing, code reviews, design guidance, and hands-on technical support, helping good engineering practices spread across the team
  • Digging into technical design and risk trade-offs — including failure modes, operational readiness, security, performance, and cost — and resolving blockers that slow the team down
  • Designing data-intensive software across relational databases such as Aurora PostgreSQL, object storage, and AWS services, with careful attention to data modelling, performance, and schema evolution at scale
  • Building software that processes data at scale on AWS using technologies such as Lambda, containerised services, and, where appropriate, Glue, EMR Serverless, and lakehouse table formats such as Apache Iceberg
  • Embedding observability, automated testing, monitoring, and quality controls so that issues are identified before they affect customers
  • Taking ownership of production outcomes and helping the team build software that is reliable, supportable, and straightforward to operate
  • Influencing and collaborating across engineering teams and translating effectively between technical and non-technical audiences
  • Building deep knowledge of the financial indices domain and using that understanding to guide technical and architectural decisions
WHAT YOU’LL BRING

Essential — this is the bar:


  • Python is our preference, but not a hard gate at this level. Either you already lead the development of production systems in Python, or you have equivalent depth in Java, C#, C, C++, Scala, Go, or Rust and are motivated to make Python your primary language here. Engineers who have worked across multiple languages often bring valuable design perspective, and we value that
  • Depth in software design and architecture — you can decompose complex problems, define appropriate boundaries and interfaces, evaluate alternatives, and clearly explain the reasoning behind your decisions
  • Strong ownership of technical and production outcomes — you take responsibility for how systems behave in production, not simply for what gets merged
  • Strong experience with relational databases such as PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL, including data modelling, query performance, scalability, and schema evolution under real production workloads
  • Solid AWS experience and strong CI/CD, automation, testing, and software delivery practices
  • Experience with data-intensive systems, including areas such as batch processing, ETL, schema evolution, data quality, and reasoning about correctness at significant scale
  • Excellent communication skills — you adapt how you explain technical decisions to different audiences and create shared understanding across engineering, product, and business stakeholders
  • A collaborative approach to engineering. You value strong teams and shared ownership over individual heroics and thrive in an Agile environment
NICE TO HAVES

Beneficial, but not what we’re screening on:

  • Apache Spark / PySpark and experience optimising large-scale distributed processing
  • Big data experience — designing and operating systems for datasets and workloads well beyond single-machine scale
  • Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, or similar open table formats and experience with lakehouse architectures, Databricks, Snowflake, or comparable data platforms
  • CI/CD tooling such as GitLab CI, Jenkins, or GitHub Actions
  • Infrastructure as code using technologies such as Terraform or AWS CDK, together with broader platform or DevOps exposures
  • Experience in financial markets, index data, investment analytics, or other data-intensive financial products

Join us and be part of a team that values innovation, engineering quality, collaboration, and continuous improvement. If you’re ready to take ownership of significant technical challenges and make a meaningful impact on software used across global financial markets, we’d love to hear from you.

Career Stage:

Manager

London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) Information:

Join us and be part of a team that values innovation, quality, and continuous improvement. If you're ready to take your career to the next level and make a significant impact, we'd love to hear from you.

LSEG is a leading global financial markets infrastructure and data provider. Our purpose is driving financial stability, empowering economies and enabling customers to create sustainable growth.

Our purpose is the foundation on which our culture is built. Our values of Integrity, Partnership, Excellence and Change underpin our purpose and set the standard for everything we do, every day. They go to the heart of who we are and guide our decision making and everyday actions.

Working with us means that you will be part of a dynamic organisation of 25,000 people across 65 countries. However, we will value your individuality and enable you to bring your true self to work so you can help enrich our diverse workforce.

We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer. This means that we do not discriminate on the basis of anyone’s race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. Conforming with applicable law, we can reasonably accommodate applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs.

You will be part of a collaborative and creative culture where we encourage new ideas. We are committed to sustainability across our global business and we are proud to partner with our customers to help them meet their sustainability objectives. Our charity, the LSEG Foundation provides charitable grants to community groups that help people access economic opportunities and build a secure future with financial independence. Colleagues can get involved through fundraising and volunteering.

LSEG offers a range of tailored benefits and support, including healthcare, retirement planning, paid volunteering days and wellbeing initiatives.

title: Engineering Manager
description:
Company Description

Every day, millions of people do their work in the same few tools: where they write, share, plan and ask for help. When those tools are hard to use, people lose time searching, guessing and asking around. At Caelor, we build apps that make that everyday work simpler, so teams can find what they need, understand it quickly and get on with their job.

Our apps run inside Atlassian’s products (Jira and Confluence), used by companies all over the world. They turn Confluence into a real company intranet, make pages clear and easy to read, explain internal vocabulary right where people need it, and give every employee a simple way to request the equipment and services they need.

Caelor brings together the Vectors and Caelor teams under one name: about 40 people across Tunis, Paris, Wiesbaden, Split and Dubai, with Tunis as our largest office. We value collaboration across teams and countries, honest feedback, and a transparent, friendly way of working.

Job Description

About the role

Caelor builds apps that make Atlassian work the way people do, because tools should adapt to people, not the other way around. We’re looking for an Engineering Manager to lead our delivery organization: about 15 people across product development squads, QA, release management and AI engineering. You’ll report to the CTO and own how we ship, so that every release of our Atlassian Marketplace apps is high quality and on schedule. You’ll also be the person engineers turn to for growth, feedback and removing obstacles.

This is a full-time management role. You won’t write production code day to day, but you’ll stay close enough to the technical work to understand trade-offs, challenge estimates and earn the trust of the engineers you lead.

What you’ll do

  • Lead people: manage and coach the two squad leads, run 1:1s, performance reviews and development plans, and build a culture of ownership.
  • Hire and onboard: own hiring for delivery, QA and release roles, and get newcomers productive fast.
  • Own delivery: planning, estimation, sprint cadence and releases, with a lightweight process shared across squads. Track predictability (cycle time, commitment accuracy, escaped defects).
  • Raise quality: manage the QA and Release Manager, move us toward automated testing, and run blameless post-incident reviews.
  • Coordinate: resolve priority and resource clashes between squads, and work with the Tech Lead and R&D on standards, security fixes and bringing prototypes (including AI) to production.

Qualifications

What we’re looking for

  • 3+ years managing software engineers (1:1s, reviews, hiring)
  • An engineering background strong enough to discuss architecture and technical debt
  • A track record of improving delivery predictability in agile teams, with concrete examples
  • Hands-on experience with QA practices, CI/CD and release processes
  • Direct communication: comfortable giving hard feedback and pushing back on unrealistic deadlines
  • Fluent English

Nice to have

  • Atlassian Marketplace apps (Forge, Connect, Data Center)
  • Managing team leads or several teams
  • Leading a move from manual to automated testing
  • SaaS experience with SOC 2, ISO 27001 or GDPR

Additional Information

What's in for you:

  • Attractive remuneration
  • Lunch voucher
  • Medical insurance
  • Annual performance bonuses
  • Flexible work hours
  • Hydride remote
  • 25 days: paid leave
  • Team building activities
  • Are you a geeky mom? You will keep your salary during your maternity leave and we are addressing flexible hours for working mums!

title: Staff Product Engineer (Backend)

description:
At Moxie, we empower ambitious aesthetic entrepreneurs to build profitable, independent practices—without burnout, overwhelm, or guesswork. In just a few years, we've grown from an idea to a global, remote-first team now supporting 700+ practices nationwide.

Our purpose is simple: to unlock sustainable success for aesthetic entrepreneurs, at every stage of their journey.

Staff Product Engineer (Backend)

We're looking for a Staff Product Engineer (Backend) to lead some of Moxie's highest-impact projects in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027, starting on our Financial Operations (FinOps) team. Beyond the project work, you'll provide technical leadership across the company and own and validate the major architectural decisions that shape how Moxie builds. This hire is part of a deliberate shift toward direct-hire engineers in the Americas, and you'll help set the engineering standards for the team

You'll join FinOps as a core contributor and work day to day with Product, Design, and your engineering peers on the payments and transactions systems that our customers rely on, including our integrations with Stripe, LayerFi, and Cherry. You'll work across our middleware and backend architecture, key GraphQL schemas, APIs, and data models, and

Our Objectives for the Role

  • Become a primary IC on FinOps by the end of Q4. Within three months you're ramped on FinOps workflows, the middleware and backend architecture, and Moxie's release practices, and you contribute a meaningful share of overall project velocity.

  • Ship early wins that make the backend better. In your first three months, deliver targeted fixes and improvements that raise reliability, performance, or developer experience, and address a clear backend pain point raised by engineers, product, or our customers

  • Lead a big project from design to production. Take one meaningful FinOps project through design, architecture review, cross-functional collaboration, and launch, then lead a second, more ambitious initiative to a visible milestone or production-ready state by month six.

  • Shape architecture across the company. Within three months you're ramped to Moxie's system design and architecture, and opinionated on what we can do better, and what we should build next. You're comfortable developing technical proposals, and taking them from draft to review, approval, and final implementation.

  • Own non-project technical initiatives and engineering culture. Start owning at least one org-level initiative in your first three months (for example unit testing standards, redesigning our SDLC for the agentic era, documentation culture, or the code review process), and by month nine own one or two initiatives with measurable gains in quality or velocity, while shipping v1 of one or more key initiatives.

We're Looking For

  • 8-12 years of backend engineering experience, including time at the senior or staff level leading large initiatives and influencing architecture across teams

  • Staff-level backend experience. You've led large, ambiguous initiatives as a hands-on IC, owning scope, delivery, and tradeoffs, and you want to do it again with clear accountability.

  • Depth in financial, payments, or transactions systems. You've built and shipped systems where money moves and correctness matters, and you can learn a new domain and its business context quickly.

  • Strong backend and API design judgment. You're comfortable across middleware, GraphQL schemas, APIs, and data models, and you can explain the design choices and tradeoffs behind them.

  • A record of influencing architecture. You've made and defended major architectural decisions, and you balance speed, quality, and long-term maintainability when you plan with product and engineering leadership.

  • Ownership of engineering standards. You've established or matured practices such as unit testing, code review, documentation, or SDLC automation, and you lead by modeling them.

  • Cross-functional partnership. You work closely with Product, Design, and engineering peers, unblock complex decisions across teams, and communicate status, risks, and tradeoffs clearly.

  • Fluency with AI tooling in daily work. You use AI tools in how you build and have a point of view on how AI can improve the software development lifecycle. Bonus points if you’re opinionated about harnesses, tooling (Ghosty, Herdr, Pi, Plannotator, etc), and multi-agent workflows and processes.

This is not a role for someone who wants a narrow, single-system scope or a title without hands-on delivery.

Why Join Us?

  • Real ownership and influence. You'll operate as a high-trust IC with a real say in architecture and technical direction, on decisions that aren't buried under layers of bureaucracy.

  • Ambitious financial systems used by real customers. You'll build and ship payments and transactions products at meaningful scale, with real complexity and real constraints.

  • Shape how engineering works. You'll help set the cultural norms and build the processes where they aren't yet in place, not just ship features.

title: Fatherhood Specialist
description:
Job Description

At Child Development Resources (CDR), we believe every child deserves a strong start—and that strong families are built through meaningful relationships, positive parenting, and supportive communities. We are a mission-driven nonprofit dedicated to empowering children and families through early intervention, family support, prevention, and community-based services.

We are seeking an engaging, compassionate, and relationship-driven Fatherhood Specialist to join our Fatherhood First program. This is an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of fathers, children, and families by helping men develop the confidence, skills, and resources they need to become involved, responsible, and nurturing parents.

The ideal candidate is an enthusiastic communicator, skilled facilitator, and natural relationship-builder who enjoys working directly with people. We are looking for someone who can inspire fathers, create welcoming learning environments, build trust, and connect families with resources that promote long-term success.

Reporting to the Fatherhood Project Director, the Fatherhood Specialist provides educational workshops, individualized mentoring, case management, and community outreach throughout the Hampton Roads region.

Most importantly, this position offers the opportunity to help fathers strengthen their relationships with their children, build healthier families, and create a positive impact that lasts for generations.

About the Role

The Fatherhood Specialist plays an important role in CDR's Fatherhood First program, which promotes responsible fatherhood, positive parenting, healthy relationships, effective co-parenting, and economic stability.

Through group workshops, individual guidance, and community partnerships, the Fatherhood Specialist helps fathers and father figures develop practical skills, overcome challenges, and become more confident and engaged in their children's lives.

This position combines education, mentoring, case management, and community engagement. Successful candidates will be equally comfortable facilitating an interactive workshop, listening to a father's concerns, helping someone establish personal goals, or collaborating with community organizations to identify resources and opportunities.

The Fatherhood Specialist will work closely with the Fatherhood Project Director, program staff, and community partners to support program success and meaningful outcomes for participating families.

What You Will Do

Fatherhood Education & Workshop Facilitation

  • Plan, organize, and facilitate engaging educational workshops using the nationally recognized 24/7 Dad™ curriculum.

  • Create a welcoming, supportive, and interactive learning environment that encourages participation and personal growth.

  • Help fathers strengthen parenting skills, understand child development, and develop positive relationships with their children.

  • Facilitate discussions about responsible fatherhood, healthy relationships, effective communication, co-parenting, and family stability.

  • Encourage fathers to apply newly developed skills and strategies in their everyday lives.

Individual Mentoring & Case Management

  • Provide individualized guidance, encouragement, and case management services to participating fathers.

  • Build trusting, respectful relationships that help fathers identify their strengths, needs, challenges, and personal goals.

  • Support fathers in developing practical strategies to strengthen family relationships, improve economic stability, and achieve greater self-sufficiency.

  • Connect participants with community resources, including employment assistance, financial counseling, housing support, childcare, and family services.

  • Monitor participant progress and maintain accurate, confidential case management records.

  • Follow organizational and program requirements related to confidentiality, participant safety, domestic violence screening, and reporting suspected abuse or neglect.

Community Outreach & Engagement

  • Build positive relationships with community organizations, service providers, and referral partners.

  • Participate in outreach and recruitment activities to connect fathers and father figures with program services.

  • Collaborate with community partners to identify resources and opportunities that support participating families.

  • Represent Fatherhood First and CDR professionally at community meetings, events, and outreach activities.

  • Help increase awareness of the importance of responsible fatherhood and the positive impact of involved fathers on children and families.

Program Collaboration & Accountability

  • Collaborate with the Fatherhood Project Director and program staff to coordinate services, establish priorities, and support program goals.

  • Maintain timely and accurate documentation of workshops, participant services, and program activities.

  • Assist in monitoring program progress, timelines, and evaluation outcomes.

  • Follow CDR policies and applicable federal grant requirements.

  • Participate in team meetings, professional development opportunities, and program-related conferences and training.

Minimum Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent.

  • Experience presenting, teaching, or facilitating workshops, classes, or group discussions.

  • Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.

  • Demonstrated ability to build positive relationships with individuals from diverse backgrounds and life experiences.

  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple responsibilities.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and Outlook.

  • Ability and willingness to travel frequently throughout the Hampton Roads region to facilitate workshops, conduct outreach, and provide case management services.

  • Must possess a valid driver's license and provide a current driving record demonstrating an acceptable driving history in accordance with CDR's insurance requirements.

  • Flexibility to accommodate occasional evening workshops and communication with program participants.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in fatherhood programs, family support services, parenting education, mentoring, case management, or community outreach.

  • Experience working with fathers, families, or individuals facing economic or social challenges.

  • Familiarity with community resources and support services throughout Hampton Roads.

  • Experience facilitating parenting education or other evidence-based educational programs.

  • Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish.

Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate is a compassionate, enthusiastic, and approachable professional who genuinely enjoys helping others grow and succeed.

They understand that meaningful change begins with trust, encouragement, and positive relationships. They are comfortable engaging groups, facilitating conversations, listening without judgment, and helping individuals develop practical solutions to everyday challenges.

They bring energy and creativity to educational workshops, patience and empathy to individual mentoring, and professionalism to interactions with community partners.

They are organized, dependable, and committed to maintaining accurate records while balancing the personal connections that make this work meaningful.

Above all, they believe in the importance of involved fathers and understand that supporting fathers is an investment in stronger children, healthier families, and more resilient communities.

Compensation

Annual Salary: $50,000

This is a full-time position offering a competitive total compensation package, including comprehensive benefits, generous paid leave, retirement contributions, and opportunities for professional development.

Work Location & Travel

This position is based at CDR's Williamsburg campus, located at 312 Waller Mill Road, Williamsburg, Virginia.

The Fatherhood Specialist works directly with fathers, families, and community partners throughout the Hampton Roads region. Frequent regional travel is an essential responsibility of this position.

Candidates must possess a valid driver's license and provide a current driving record that meets CDR's insurance eligibility standards.

Why Work at CDR?

Make a Meaningful Difference: Help fathers strengthen their relationships with their children, develop positive parenting skills, and build healthier, more stable families.

Competitive Total Compensation: Enjoy an annual salary of $50,000, comprehensive benefits, generous paid leave, and programs designed to support employees personally and professionally.

Exceptional Retirement Benefit: CDR provides a 6% non-contributory 401(k) contribution of your compensation, subject to a three-year vesting period.

Outstanding Benefits: Enjoy health, dental, and vision insurance, generous paid time off and holidays, and paid Spring and Winter breaks.

Professional Growth: Expand your skills in education, mentoring, family support, and community engagement while working alongside dedicated professionals.

A Collaborative, Supportive Environment: Join a team that values relationships, creativity, collaboration, and the contributions of every employee.

Work-Life Balance: Be part of an organization that recognizes the importance of supporting employees' personal well-being and professional success.

Join Our Team

If you are a passionate communicator, enthusiastic educator, and compassionate relationship-builder who wants to make a meaningful difference in the lives of fathers and families, we invite you to bring your talents to CDR.

Help fathers discover their strengths, build stronger connections with their children, and create a lasting legacy of positive parenting.

Apply today and become part of CDR's Fatherhood First team!


Child Development Resources is a Drug-Free Workplace and Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Logistics Coordinator 1 (61391)
description:
The Logistics Coordinator I supports accurate, on-time customer order fulfillment from order receipt through delivery for Tofurky. This role processes and maintains order and shipment information, coordinates routine shipping activities, and communicates order status and product availability to customers and internal teams. The Coordinator also supports the investigation, documentation, and resolution of customer deductions, chargebacks, carrier claims, and other shipment-related discrepancies.

Essential Functions

  • Process and maintain customer orders in the company’s ERP system, EDI platform, and customer portals, verifying order details, requested dates, quantities, ship-to information, and customer requirements.
  • Monitor open orders, product availability, and shipment status; identify potential shortages or delays and coordinate timely updates with Customer Service, Sales, Supply Chain, and other internal teams.
  • Coordinate routine carrier pickups, shipment scheduling, delivery appointments, and shipment tracking with carriers, customers, and logistics partners.
  • Prepare and verify fulfillment documentation and transaction information, including bills of lading, shipment confirmations, advance ship notices, and proof of delivery.
  • Follow up on routine order and shipment exceptions, gather supporting records, and escalate unresolved service, delivery, or compliance issues to the Supply Chain Manager.
  • Assist with investigating, documenting, and disputing carrier charges, customer fines, chargebacks, deductions, and related claims in coordination with the Supply Chain Manager.
  • Maintain accurate order, shipment, customer, and item information in applicable systems and shared trackers.
  • Support customer setup and maintenance by gathering requirements, maintaining routing and shipping instructions, and following up on EDI and customer-portal issues.
  • Prepare routine fulfillment and logistics reporting and help identify recurring errors and opportunities for process improvement.
  • Coordinate with third-party logistics providers on day-to-day order and shipment execution, referring broader partner or relationship matters to the appropriate team lead.

Responsibilities

  • Inspects deliveries, verifies quantities and documentation against requisitions, invoices, and shipping records, and works with suppliers to resolve discrepancies.

  • Conducts routine inventory counts and audits, identifies variances, and supports discrepancy resolution.

  • Prepares procurement requests for materials and supplies.

  • Marks materials with identifying information as required.

  • Operates forklifts as needed to move materials safely and efficiently.

  • Maintains a clean, organized, and safe warehouse environment.

  • High school diploma.

  • Minimum of 1 year of experience in a similar role.

  • Knowledge of materials and hardware handling.

  • Basic understanding of inventory control procedures.

  • Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Word.

  • Experience operating a forklift and ability to obtain Karman forklift certification.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience using Epicor or another enterprise resource planning (ERP) system.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to navigate all areas of the facility and reach items at various heights.

  • Ability to stand, walk, or sit for at least 8 hours.

  • Ability to occasionally push, pull, lift, or carry 25–50 pounds.

  • Ability to occasionally climb stairs or ramps.

title: Systems Support & Integration Engineer-USV
location: BlueOps - Fort Pierce - Fort Pierce, FL 34946-7331
description:
Position Summary

Blue Ops designs, builds, and fields autonomous unmanned surface vessels (USVs) for

defense and national security customers. We are seeking a hands-on Systems Support &

Integration Engineer to support the integration, troubleshooting, testing, and fielding of

complex unmanned vessel systems.

This role is well suited for an engineer with a computer engineering, electrical engineering, IT,

robotics, or related technical background who enjoys diagnosing problems across software,

networks, electronics, sensors, and physical hardware. The successful candidate will work

directly with onboard compute, communications equipment, cameras, radar, GNSS, autopilot

hardware, vessel networks, power systems, and other integrated electronics.

The focus of this position is system diagnosis and troubleshooting. This engineer is expected

to approach problems methodically, determine whether a failure originates in software,

configuration, networking, power, wiring, hardware, or an interface between systems, and

drive the issue through verification and resolution.

This is a hands-on role. The engineer should be equally comfortable working from a Linux

terminal, checking device connectivity, reviewing logs, and validating configurations as they

are using a multimeter, inspecting wiring, replacing hardware, or working aboard a vessel

during integration and test.

Key Responsibilities

• Diagnose and resolve faults across USV onboard systems, including compute, sensors,

communications, cameras, radar, GNSS, autopilot hardware, vessel networks, and

supporting electronics.

• Perform structured troubleshooting of hardware, software, configuration, networking,

power, wiring, sensor, and system-integration issues.

• Determine root cause rather than relying solely on component swapping or temporary

workarounds.

• Support vessel system checkout before testing, demonstrations, deliveries, and

customer events.

• Verify that onboard systems are communicating, configured correctly, and operating as

expected prior to deployment.

Ft. Pierce, FL (On-site / In person)

• Review system logs, service status, device health, and other diagnostic information to

isolate failures.

• Troubleshoot Linux-based onboard computers and embedded systems using tools such

as SSH, command-line utilities, logs, and system services.

• Perform basic network troubleshooting involving IP addressing, Ethernet connectivity,

static IPs, DHCP, switches, and device-to-device communications.

• Perform low-voltage DC electrical troubleshooting using a multimeter, including

verification of power, continuity, grounding, fuses, relays, connectors, and wiring.

• Identify recurring system issues and work with engineering teams to develop durable

corrective actions.

Required Qualifications

• 1-4 years of experience in systems support, integration, field engineering, test

engineering, robotics, embedded systems, IT/OT, or a related technical role.

• Strong hands-on troubleshooting skills across hardware, software, networking, power,

wiring, and configuration.

• Working familiarity with Linux, SSH, command-line tools, logs, and basic system

configuration.

• Basic networking knowledge including IP addressing, Ethernet, DHCP, and static IP

configuration.

• Ability to use a multimeter and troubleshoot basic low-voltage DC electrical systems.

• Comfortable physically working on electronics and equipment aboard small vessels.

• Ability to read wiring diagrams, network diagrams, technical manuals, and interface

documentation.

• U.S. citizenship and ability to obtain and maintain a DoD security clearance.

• Ability to travel up to 50%.

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems

Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, IT, or similar.

• Experience with USVs, UAS, UGVs, robotics, marine electronics, defense, aerospace,

automotive, or other complex integrated systems.

• Experience with NVIDIA Jetson, Raspberry Pi, or other embedded Linux systems.

• Familiarity with radar, cameras, GNSS/INS, Starlink, RF communications, CAN,

NMEA 2000, or serial interfaces.

• Experience with ArduPilot, ArduRover, PX4, MAVLink, or Pixhawk.

• Experience with Wireshark or similar troubleshooting tools.

• Experience with field testing, demonstrations, commissioning, or deployed systems.

Travel & Working Conditions

• Up to 50% travel, including customer sites, test ranges, partner locations, and potential

OCONUS travel.

• Early starts, extended days, and occasional weekend work may be required around test

events.

• Must be comfortable working aboard vessels, outdoors, dockside, and in shop/test

environments.

• Must be able to kneel, crouch, climb, access installed equipment, and lift

approximately 25 lbs.

Physical Requirements and Working Environment

This role combines office and laboratory work with hands-on vessel integration and outdoor testing.

• Ability to manually lift and carry equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds.

• Ability to crawl, kneel, crouch, bend, climb, and work in confined or awkward spaces while installing, inspecting, and servicing equipment on and around vessels.

• Ability to safely board and move around boats, docks, and uneven or wet surfaces.

• Comfortable working outdoors and in marine environments, including dockside activities and on-water testing.

• Occasional travel and schedule flexibility may be required to support trials and demonstrations.

Background Check

This position will require successfully completing a post-offer background check. Qualified candidates with a criminal history will be considered and are not automatically disqualified, consistent with federal and state law.

EEO and ITAR/EAR Work Authorization Disclosure

Red Cat Holdings provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. This position requires direct or indirect access to hardware, software, technology or technical data controlled under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Successful candidates for positions subject to ITAR/EAR restrictions must provide proof of U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residence and must not require sponsorship for export-restricted work authorization.

The company participates E-Verify ensure eligibility for employment and compliance with Right to Work rules.

TBG Overview:

title: Healthcare Advocacy - Clinical Director
description:
🏥 About Sailor Health

For most older adults, healthcare doesn’t fail in one place—it fails across many. Mental health, physical health, medications, and day-to-day realities all interact, but the system treats them separately. The result is confusion, missed care, and worsening outcomes.

Sailor Health is building a new model of care for older adults that brings the mind and the body together. We combine healthcare advocacy, behavioral health, and wellness classes to help patients and families understand what’s going on and what to do next. By taking a more holistic and preventative approach, we aim to catch issues earlier, reduce avoidable crises, and keep patients in their homes instead of the hospital.

⭐ About the Role

Location: Remote – US based

Sailor’s physicians are the clinical gateway for patients navigating chronic conditions and complex care needs. Through telehealth visits, they assess the full medical picture and partner with healthcare advocates to build care plans patients can actually follow. While our therapists lead the work on the mind, our physicians lead the clinical perspective on the body.

As Healthcare Advocacy - Clinical Director, you will lead this physician group. You will shape what our physicians do, how they do it, and how we scale it while keeping the quality bar high. You will own physician hiring and onboarding, run day-to-day clinical operations, build the care model and protocols that make the advocacy program work, and be the person our physicians turn to when a case gets hard.

This is a builder’s role. You will be one of the first clinical leaders at Sailor and you will have a direct hand in how the program grows from a small team today to a much larger one over the next year. We’re looking for someone who is still a strong clinician, gets energy from building systems, is comfortable with ambiguity, and wants to help create something from the ground up.

💻 Your Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the physician team: Run day-to-day clinical leadership for our telehealth physicians serving Medicare patients with chronic and complex conditions, and be the escalation point for hard cases

  • Hire, onboard, and train physicians at scale: Own physician recruiting with our Talent team, set the hiring bar, and build the onboarding program that gets new doctors productive fast

  • Build the care model for advocacy: Develop the workflows, pathways, and protocols for how physicians assess patients and partner with advocates on care plans

  • Own clinical quality and compliance: Run QA and QI programs across visits and documentation, and write the policies that keep us compliant across states

  • Measure and partner across the company: Define physician KPIs with our Data team, coach from the numbers, and turn clinical needs into priorities for Product, Growth, and Care Ops

✅ What We’re Looking For

  • Licensed and board certified: Active, unrestricted medical license with board certification in internal medicine, family medicine, or geriatrics (Ideally licensed in 30+ states)

  • A proven physician leader: 3+ years managing other physicians as a medical director or similar, with a track record of building and developing clinical teams

  • Still loves seeing patients: 5+ years of direct patient care, ideally with older adults, and excited to keep a portion of your time dedicated to patient visits

  • Thrives in ambiguity: Comfortable making decisions without a playbook, moving fast, and changing course when the evidence says so

  • Clear communicator: Can translate clinical judgment for non-clinical partners and bring teams along without pulling rank

  • Startup or digital health experience is a plus: Prior time at an early stage company or virtual care organization helps, and comfort working autonomously is a must

Are you ready to gain hands-on experience bringing ideas to life through creative display design? As our Structural Design Intern, you’ll work alongside our talented Structural Design (TPOP) team to develop, test, and refine dimensional displays for a variety of The Bernard Group’s customers. You’ll design and evaluate 3D structural concepts using ArtiosCAD software, support production teams, and gain exposure to the entire process—from concept to finished display.

On top of that you must:

  • willing to admit when you make a mistake (it happens to the best of us)

TBG Overview:

The Bernard Group, Inc.

description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies’ core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

We combine comprehensive analysis, engineering, and program execution capabilities to deliver mission-tailored solutions that reduce lead times, lower costs, and simplify complex multi-vendor supply chains. Backed by decades of flight-proven and fielded performance, we design and build mission-critical technologies including launch systems, propulsion, payload integration solutions, UAV components, missile subsystems, and Safe & Arm systems.

As a Buyer, you support production and development programs by acquiring critical materials, components, and services. title: IT Project Architect
description:
Nature and Variety of Work


Come join our team!

Prince George’s County Government provides a dynamic and inclusive workplace where employees can thrive, learn, and grow across its 30 diverse agencies, all dedicated to serving the County's residents with essential resources and services. Nestled just minutes away from Washington, DC, Prince George's County combines urban vibrancy with serene surroundings, offering an ideal setting to live, work, and enjoy life.

Applicant Limit Notice: Please be advised that applications for this position will be capped at a maximum of 100 submissions. Once this threshold has been reached, the posting will close, and no further applications will be accepted. We encourage interested candidates to apply promptly to ensure consideration.

The Prince George’s County Office of Information Technology is currently seeking qualified applicants to fill an IT Project Architect, (Info Tech Project Coordinator 4G) grade G27 position, in the Project Management Office.


About the Position
This is principal level professional and technical work responsible for all aspects of designing and implementing IT solutions for County agencies. The incumbent serves as IT strategy planner, IT architect and project Manager, responsible for supporting County agencies in researching, identifying, planning, and implementing information technology solutions that support their business mission and operational requirements. Work includes a balance of technical architecture, project governance, administration, and leadership responsibilities to include performing business analysis, identifying technology opportunities, conducting feasibility analysis, and facilitating communication with the OIT technology teams. Work is performed under general supervision of the PMO Manager while exercising a high degree of independence.

About the Agency
The Office of Information Technology (OIT) provides support for all of the agencies, departments, and branches of County government. The OIT Service Desk provides information technology support and maintenance services to Prince George’s County personnel. The Office of Information Technology is wholly dedicated to aligning technology efforts to support the strategic goals of the County. OIT will provide leadership, expertise, and resources in the ideation, development, and deployment of innovative technologies and streamlined processes to improve government efficiency, business interaction, and citizen access to government information and services.


Examples of Work

  • Lead the architectural assessment, design, and planning of complex technology solutions, ensuring alignment with enterprise standards,
    cybersecurity requirements, regulatory mandates, and business needs.
  • Engage with agency leadership, business stakeholders, and IT executives to develop and maintain enterprise technology roadmaps, strategic IT
    plans, and project portfolios aligned with organizational objectives.
  • Facilitate cross-functional solution design workshops and technical strategy sessions involving agency representatives, infrastructure teams,
    application teams, cybersecurity personnel, vendors, consultants, and executive stakeholders.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to assigned agencies in identifying technology needs, evaluating solution alternatives, and developing business cases
    and funding justifications for inclusion in annual budget requests and capital improvement programs.
  • Direct the planning, coordination, and execution of large-scale IT initiatives from concept through implementation, ensuring successful delivery of
    scope, schedule, budget, quality, and business outcomes.
  • Develop and oversee integrated project management artifacts including project charters, technical architecture documents, project plans,
    schedules, resource plans, risk registers, and governance reports.
  • Provide technical leadership and architectural oversight for enterprise projects, ensuring solution designs are scalable, secure, maintainable, and
    aligned with enterprise architecture principles.
  • Lead project governance activities, including Project Steering Committees, architecture review boards, and executive status briefings;
    communicate project progress, risks, dependencies, and recommendations to senior leadership.
  • Coordinate activities among multiple agencies, business units, IT divisions, contractors, and third-party vendors to ensure effective collaboration,
    issue resolution, and achievement of project objectives.
  • Monitor vendor and/or contractor performance, evaluate deliverables for compliance with contractual and technical requirements, and recommend corrective actions to Management when necessary.
  • Establish project scope, objectives, success metrics, and deliverables while ensuring stakeholder expectations are managed and aligned
    throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Identify, assess, and mitigate technical, operational, and organizational risks; proactively resolve project issues and conflicts to minimize impact
    on service delivery and project outcomes.
  • Ensure compliance with established OIT policies, PMO governance standards, cybersecurity frameworks, and organizational procedures.
  • Support technical reviews of proposed solutions, infrastructure designs, application architectures, cloud implementations, and system integrations to ensure adherence to enterprise standards and best practices.
  • Develop executive presentations, strategic recommendations, business communications, and briefing materials for elected officials, executive leadership, steering committees, and stakeholder groups.
  • Mentor project managers, business analysts, architects, and technical staff on project management methodologies, architecture standards, governance processes, and best practices.
  • Support the continuous maturation of the Project Management Office by improving methodologies, templates, governance frameworks, performance metrics, and enterprise project delivery capabilities.
  • Research emerging technologies, industry trends, and government IT best practices to identify opportunities for innovation, modernization, operational efficiency, and risk reduction.
  • Represent the OIT in meetings with agencies, industry partners, vendors, professional organizations, and external stakeholders. Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration, customer service, innovation, and continuous improvement while maintaining the highest standards of professionalism, ethics, confidentiality, and public stewardship.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in information technology, business or public administration or a closely related field.
  • Three (3) years of information technology experience, in which at least one (1) year must have involved lead/supervisory duties.
Any equivalent combination of relevant training, education and experience may also be considered.
Please note there is no equivalency for the required supervisory experience.

Preferred Qualifications
  • PMP – Project Management Professional (PMI Certification)
  • CBAP – Certified Business Analyst Professional (IIBA Certification)
  • ITIL 4 Foundation
EACH APPLICATION MUST INCLUDE INFORMATION THAT CLEARLY DEMONSTRATES THE ABOVE QUALIFICATIONS FOR THIS POSITION.

Additional Information

Salary Range Transparency: The salary range listed in this announcement reflects the anticipated offer range for this position. Offers made within this range are based on qualifications, experience, and internal equity.

Tentative Interview Dates: October 26 - October 27, 2026. Please note that interview dates are subject to change and only selected candidates will receive confirmation and additional details.

Conditions of Employment: Upon selection, the candidate must (where applicable):

•Meet all training and performance standards and demonstrate proficiency as required by the agency.
•Wear and use agency protective apparel and equipment in the performance of their assigned duties.
•Successfully pass preemployment checks which may include reference checks, background investigations, and drug screenings, where applicable.
•Be willing and able to serve as an essential employee. Essential employees are expected to report during standard or non-standard hours as operations necessitate, or during emergencies. Essential employees are expected to report or remain at work when other County employees are granted Administrative Leave.

ONLY ONLINE APPLICATIONS WILL BE ACCEPTED

Eligibility to Work: Under the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, an employer is required to hire only U.S. citizens and lawfully authorized alien workers. Applicants who are selected for employment will be required to provide and verify authorization to work in the United States without sponsorship.

This employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S., only after an offer has been accepted and the Form I-9 is completed. For information on E-Verify, or if you believe the County has violated its E-Verify responsibilities, please contact the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) at 888-897-7781 or visit their website at dhs.gov/E-Verify.

  • Lifting and Carrying: Ability to lift and carry heavy objects, typically up to 50 pounds, and occasionally heavier items with assistance.
  • Standing and Walking: Prolonged periods of standing and walking throughout the facility.
  • Bending and Stooping: Frequent bending, stooping, and crouching to access equipment and perform maintenance tasks.
  • Climbing: Climbing ladders and stairs to reach elevated areas and equipment.
  • Manual Dexterity: Fine motor skills for handling tools, parts, and equipment with precision.
  • Reaching: Reaching overhead and at various heights to perform tasks.
  • Pushing and Pulling: Pushing and pulling carts, tools, and equipment.
  • Kneeling and Crawling: Kneeling and crawling to access hard-to-reach areas and perform repairs.
  • Visual Acuity: Good vision to read technical manuals, schematics, and to inspect equipment.
  • Hearing: Ability to hear alarms, machinery sounds, and communicate effectively in a noisy environment.
  • Balance and Coordination: Maintaining balance and coordination while working on ladders, scaffolding, or in confined spaces

Competencies:

  • Troubleshooting: Identifying and resolving issues with oil processing machinery.
  • Documentation: Maintaining accurate records of oil processing activities and equipment performance.
  • Regulatory Knowledge: Understanding of food safety regulations and standards related to oil processing.
  • Safety Protocols: Adhering to all safety regulations and company policies.
  • Communication: Effectively communicating with team members and supervisors.
  • Time Management: Prioritizing tasks and managing time effectively to meet production schedules.
  • Inventory Management: Managing inventory of oil processing supplies and equipment.
  • Flexibility: Adapting to changes in production demands and processing requirements.

Core Responsibilities:

  • Maintain Food Safety, Food Defense and cGMP practices at all times.
  • Follow all OSHA Safety Regulation and Safety Rules.
  • Report any Safety concerns to management.
  • Ensure that all ingredient oil is received according to procedure in a sanitary manner and to the appropriate vessel.
  • Prepare and use vessels appropriately and ensure oil transfers are conducted appropriately.
  • Monitor the oil in use via testing and determine appropriate course of action such as filtering, refreshing, etc.
  • Dispose of waste ingredient oil promptly and according to procedure.
  • Clean and maintain the oil system components at designated frequency to ensure food safety and quality.
  • Additional Duties:
  1. Oil Transfers
  1. Confirm that the vessels used to make the transfer (small tanks or totes typically) are suitably cleaned, sanitized, labeled and otherwise appropriately prepared to receive the transfer.
  1. Ensure that transfer activities are conducted in a sanitary manner that does not increase the risk of contamination of the oil being transferred.
  1. Oil Monitoring and Testing
  1. Deliver samples of oil to the QA lab for FFA and moisture analysis on a prescribed frequency to maintain product quality.
  1. Collect an oil sample each day and refresh it daily for external analytical testing.
  1. Collect additional oil samples throughout the duration of accelerated oil degradation for external analytical testing.
  1. Waste Oil Disposal
  1. Ensure that materials are in place to properly collect waste oil as it is produced and actively seek ways to prevent the loss of oil from being made into waste.
  1. Ensure that waste oils are properly transported to the storage bin and inform management when the bin is ready for emptying.
  1. Oil System Cleaning
  1. To conduct all internal and external cleaning activities related to the fryers, fryer pump skids, fryer heat exchangers, fryer oil piping and storage tanks. This includes daily debriding
  1. Maintain clean and sanitize the equipment, utensils and work areas. (Boil out/ CIP)
  1. Support MSS
  1. Changeovers: assist during changeovers on TC line and Pellet line to debride fryer as this a part of the changeover paperwork and procedure.
  1. Assist with other tasks as assigned by supervisor.

title: Senior Software Developer
description:
About Contour


Contour Software has grown from a dozen people to over 2,000 staff across 3 cities, in less than 14 years.

As a subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc., we are proud to be part of a global enterprise software conglomerate that has grown to become one of the top 10 software companies in the world, with employees and customers in 100+ countries. With a broad-based and ever-growing portfolio of market-leading, vertical-market enterprise solutions covering more than 100 industry domains in predominantly mature markets, CSI's recipe creates the perfect environment for professionals to build fulfilling, long-term careers.

What started as an R&D & Accounting back-office, has progressed into a full-service Global Centre serving all functions and departments, at the divisional as well as operating group/corporate level. Today Contour employees, located in Karachi, Lahore & Islamabad, are serving CSI divisions located in time zones spanning the globe, from Sydney to Vancouver. With the global growth of Constellation as the wind in our sails, we are only just getting started!

Role summary

We're hiring a senior developer for our Desktop team. The team owns our current desktop products, which are Windows applications built on Visual Basic 6 (VB6) and COM, and which customers depend on every day, while CalcAir builds modern web versions of those products.

This is a lasting senior role for an engineer who knows VB6 deeply and uses AI tools to understand, document, and safely improve existing code. Our desktop products will stay in service for as long as customers depend on them, and you'll help keep them reliable, make the team's day-to-day work smoother, and help plan the path from VB6 to the web.

We're adopting an AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) approach, where AI takes on more of the analysis and building while engineers set direction, review the work, and make the decisions that matter. You'll work with our Desktop Team Lead and the Desktop team, with Product, and with Infrastructure & IT on builds and releases.
What you'll accomplish in your first year

  • First 90 days: Learn our VB6 codebase and the business rules behind it. Use Claude Code to map the highest-risk areas and document how they work. Get comfortable with our GitHub and Azure DevOps (ADO) workflows, and note where the team's process creates the most friction.
  • By 6 months: Add tests around critical workflows so changes are safer. Lead a set of fixes or improvements from planning through release, using AI-DLC checkpoints. Make the first improvements to how we build, test, and release. Share practical AI techniques for legacy code with the team.
  • By 12 months: Help define the path from our VB6 products to the web, including which business rules to carry forward and which to rebuild. Deliver the first meaningful piece of that work, and keep improving how the team works along the way.


Responsibilities

Desktop product support

  • Lead the technical work on VB6 desktop products, including defect fixes, enhancements, and releases.
  • Serve as the senior technical resource for hard problems and critical customer issues.
  • Keep current products stable, supportable, and documented for as long as customers depend on them.

Process and workflow improvement

  • Find and fix the slow, manual, or error-prone steps in how we build, test, and release desktop products.
  • Improve how we use GitHub and Azure DevOps (ADO), so work is tracked, reviewed, and released consistently.
  • Use Claude Code to automate repetitive work in analysis, testing, and documentation.
  • Turn what works into shared team practices, so the whole team benefits.

Legacy code understanding and modernization

  • Use Claude Code to analyze VB6 code: map workflows, extract business rules, and identify risk before changes are made.
  • Write and maintain characterization tests that capture current behavior, so the web versions can be checked against it.
  • Work with Product to decide which business rules and behaviors carry forward into the web products.

AI-assisted development

  • Use Claude Code as a regular part of your daily work for analysis, changes, tests, and documentation.
  • Apply AI-DLC practices and help the Desktop team use AI safely on legacy code.
  • Review AI-generated changes carefully, especially in code with little test coverage.

Collaboration and delivery

  • Work in GitHub for source control and pull requests, and in Azure DevOps (ADO) for work items and tracking.
  • Partner with Infrastructure & IT on builds, releases, and environments.
  • Mentor Desktop team members and document what you learn, so it isn't held by one person.

Required qualifications

  • 6+ years of professional software development, including substantial production work in VB6.
  • Deep understanding of Windows desktop application architecture, data access, and debugging VB6 applications.
  • Strong working knowledge of the COM model, ActiveX components, the Windows registry, and how legacy 32-bit applications behave on modern Windows systems.
  • Experience reading and documenting large legacy codebases, and turning them into clear descriptions of how things work.
  • Daily, hands-on use of Claude Code or a comparable agentic coding tool, with examples you can walk us through.
  • A working understanding of AI-DLC and how it applies to legacy work.
  • Experience with GitHub and Azure DevOps (ADO).
  • A track record of improving team processes and workflows, such as build, test, and release steps, and making the changes stick.
  • Senior-level judgment: you can weigh risk, explain tradeoffs to non-technical leaders, and say when something should wait.

Nice to have

  • Experience migrating VB6 or other legacy Windows applications to .NET or the web.
  • Experience with .NET/C#, React, or SQL Server, to help with the path to the web.
  • Experience writing characterization or regression tests for legacy systems.
  • Experience building AI-assisted workflows for a team, such as custom skills, agents, or MCP integrations.
  • Experience with Azure DevOps (ADO) pipelines.

Exciting Benefits we offer:

  • Market-leading Salary
  • Medical Coverage – Self & Dependents
  • Parents Medical Coverage
  • Provident Fund
  • Employee Performance-based bonuses
  • Home Internet Subsidy
  • Conveyance Allowance
  • Profit Sharing Plan [Tenured Employees Only]

  • Professional Development Budget
  • Recreational area for in-house games
  • Sporadic On-shore training opportunities
  • Friendly work environment

We’re committed to fostering a culture of respect that thrives on the varied perspectives and experiences of all individuals we recruit, employ, promote, and compensate. title: Enrollment Coordinator (Bilingual)
description:
ENROLLMENT COORDINATOR (BILINGUAL)

Since 1877, The Fresh Air Fund (Fresh Air) has been a leading youth development organization providing transformative opportunities for children and young adults from New York City's underserved communities. Rooted in the belief that access to nature and outdoor experiences can change lives, Fresh Air connects young people to the outdoors while providing opportunities for personal growth, leadership development and exploration. Through free summer camp and year-round leadership development, educational enrichment and career exploration programs, Fresh Air helps young people develop the skills, confidence and connections they need to thrive.


Serving more than 1.8 million children throughout its history, Fresh Air remains committed to expanding access to life-changing experiences that empower young people to reach their full potential. At Fresh Air, employees are driven by purpose, collaboration and a shared commitment to creating opportunities that help young people succeed.

Position Summary

The Enrollment Coordinator leads efforts to connect children and families across New York City with Fresh Air programs through strategic school partnerships, community-based outreach, and family enrollment support. This role is responsible for building and managing relationships with schools, community organizations, family-serving agencies, and other high-impact referral partners to increase awareness, applications, and participation in Fresh Air's programs.


Reporting to the Director of Enrollment, the Enrollment Coordinator plays a key role in ensuring children and families can successfully navigate the enrollment process and access Fresh Air opportunities. Responsibilities include developing and maintaining school and community partnerships; conducting outreach, presentations, and enrollment events; supporting families through the application and placement process; providing bilingual translation and interpretation services; and collaborating across departments to achieve enrollment and participation goals.

Responsibilities

  • Cultivate, manage, and strengthen partnerships with schools, after-school programs, community-based organizations, health providers, libraries, and other family-serving institutions to expand enrollment and increase access to Fresh Air programs among NYC children and families.
  • Develop relationships with high-impact referral partners that provide access to large numbers of children and families across New York City.
  • Support families throughout the enrollment process and connects participants with resources that help ensure a successful program experience.
  • Lead community engagement initiatives, including presentations, special events, outreach campaigns, and partnership driven recruitment efforts.
  • Recruit, train, and support community ambassadors who promote Fresh Air’s programs within their neighborhoods.
  • Facilitate presentations to parents and caregivers to encourage applications for Fresh Air’s summer opportunities; host community-based registration and orientation events.
  • Provide bilingual (English/Spanish) translation and interpretation support for families and partners to ensure language accessible communication, documents, and outreach materials.
  • Review applications and support families throughout the application process.
  • Train and supervise seasonal staff, interns, and volunteers for presentations, outreach, and application support activities.
  • Assist with the placement of children into Fresh Air’s programs in alignment with program capacity and participant needs.
  • Provide parents with guidance as they prepare for their child’s summer experience.
  • Coordinate and support project-based outreach efforts, including timeline development, logistics coordination, and cross-departmental communication.
  • Travel throughout NYC's five boroughs and attend evening and weekend meetings and events as needed.

Summer Expectations

  • Assist with overall Fresh Air program management needs as determined by the Director of Enrollment.

Other responsibilities as assigned.


Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree required.
  • Two to five years of experience in community outreach, community engagement, customer service, or related work serving NYC families.
  • Prior supervisory experience required.
  • Enthusiastic, teamwork-oriented, with strong interpersonal and customer service skills.
  • Bilingual: able to communicate effectively in both English and Spanish, with strong public speaking, written, and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving skills; able to plan and balance multiple projects and partnerships.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Strong computer skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and experience with databases; Salesforce experience a plus.
  • Demonstrated tact, diplomacy, cultural competence, and flexibility.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines.
  • Ability to use independent judgement.
  • Project coordination or project management experience preferred.
  • Genuine interest in youth development and supporting Fresh Air’s mission and vision.
  • As part of our commitment to maintaining a safe and healthy workplace, Fresh Air requires all employees to meet applicable vaccination requirements in accordance with federal, state, and local laws. As new public health issues arise, Fresh Air may require additional vaccinations. Proof of vaccination or an approved exemption will be required as a condition of employment, if applicable.

This “at-will” position is full-time, based in our New York City office, and currently requires three days a week in the office. Fresh Air offices are open and available all week, and all employees are permitted and encouraged to come to the office to work. Fresh Air may modify its remote work policy generally or with respect to any position at any time.


Salary & Benefits

The salary for this “at-will” position is $60,000-$70,000, commensurate with experience. Fresh Air offers a generous benefits package including medical, dental and vision insurance, flexible spending accounts, commuter benefits, and employer and employee retirement contribution plans.

Application Instructions: To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter. We are hiring on a rolling basis and encourage interested applicants to apply as early as possible. No calls or recruiters, please.
