title: AI Inference Optimization Engineer
description:
Quadric is redefining edge AI with the industry's first General Purpose Neural Processing Unit (GPNPU), enabling developers to run both neural network inference and conventional C++ code on a single programmable architecture. Our technology powers intelligent edge devices across automotive, industrial, robotics, and embedded systems.

Founded in 2016 and based in downtown Burlingame, California, Quadric is building the world's first supercomputer designed for the real-time needs of edge devices. Quadric aims to empower developers in every industry with superpowers to create tomorrow's technology, today. The company was co-founded by technologists from MIT and Carnegie Mellon, who were previously the technical co-founders of the Bitcoin computing company 21.

The Opportunity

As a member of our AI Application team, you'll own getting the latest AI models running fast and accurately on the GPNPU, from CNN perception models to LLMs and VLAs for automotive, robotics and AI-PC. You'll profile real workloads, write and tune kernels, choose quantization strategies, and build the tools that make model deployment repeatable.

What You'll Do

Analyze and optimize performance on GPNPU

  • Deploy and profile models on GPNPU, from vision/perception to LLM/VLM/VLA

  • Analyze the accuracy and choose the best quantization scheme

  • Write and tune kernels and optimize model compute graphs on GPNPU, balance speed and accuracy

Create efficient flows to convert and deploy models on GPNPU

  • Develop efficient tools and flows to speed up the model deployment, including profiling, tracing, visualization tools to find bottlenecks and agentic automation

  • Customize open-source model optimization/quantization tools

  • Integrate and automate model pruning, sparsification, quantization in the workflow

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 6-12 months, you’ll:

  • Deploy 5 new models on GPNPU independently, meeting accuracy targets

  • Deliver a 2x speedup on a model through kernel, model compression or dispatch work

  • Ship a deployment or an optimization tool the team uses every day

What We're Looking For

Required

  • 3+ years experience in AI model deployment or kernel optimization

  • BS/MS in CS/CE or related fields

  • Strong C/C++ and Python

  • Hands-on performance analysis: profilers, roofline/bandwidth reasoning, finding compute vs memory bottlenecks

  • Hands-on experience with quantization (PTQ/QAT, int8/int4) and debugging accuracy loss

  • Has written performance-critical kernels (CUDA, Triton, OpenCL, SIMD intrinsics or DSP)

Fluent with AI coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor), and interested in building agent-driven workflows for kernel and model bring-up

Preferred

  • Hands-on experience in pruning and sparsification

  • Solid understanding of accelerator microarchitecture (memory hierarchy, DMA)

  • Solid understanding of fixed-point and numerics, mixed precision

  • Understanding of compiler code generation and kernel scheduling

What We Offer

The base salary range for this position is $160,000 to $195,000. This range reflects the full span of levels and geographies at which Quadric hires for this role. The actual base salary offered will depend on a number of factors, including the specific level of the role, years and depth of relevant experience, technical skills and competencies, the criticality of the role to the business, internal equity, and work location. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for equity and a discretionary annual performance bonus as applicable to the role and level.

In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a variety of benefits to support your needs. The benefits below reflect our US-based offerings; for roles in other locations, benefits vary and are shared during the hiring process. These include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance from day one - Premiums covered at 99% for Employees

  • Company-paid life Insurance

  • Voluntary supplemental life insurance

  • STD + LTD insurance

  • Commuter support including parking or Caltrain reimbursement. Our office is conveniently located within walking distance of the Caltrain station

  • FSA + HSA

  • Equity with the business

  • Paid Parental Leave

  • 401(k) Retirement Plan

  • Flexible PTO

  • Winter holiday shutdown

  • Catered lunch each day in our office

  • Downtown Burlingame office location, close to shops, cafes, and local amenities

  • Collaborative, low-ego culture with significant ownership and impact

  • A work culture focused on innovative disruption

If this role resonates with you, we encourage you to apply even if your experience does not perfectly match every qualification. We value potential, curiosity, and a willingness to learn just as much as direct experience.

title: Control Room Operator
description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is seeking a seasoned Control Room Operator (CRO) to coordinate all on-shift operations at our power facility. This senior-level role is primarily responsible for the safe operation of all plant equipment across a variety of scenarios, ranging from cold plant startups to emergency operations during plant upsets. You will serve as an individual contributor within the Operations & Maintenance Department, making critical decisions on non-routine or escalated technical issues with limited supervision.

The ideal candidate possesses excellent troubleshooting, diagnosis, and leadership skills, with a proven track record of using Distributive Control Systems (DCS) to monitor and adjust operating parameters. This role is vital for ensuring compliance with all local, State, and Federal regulations while driving plant efficiency and safety. (#INDMFG)

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Operational Coordination: Lead the coordination of all on-shift operations, ensuring the safe operation of plant equipment during normal and emergency scenarios.

  • System Monitoring & Control: Use Distributive Control System (DCS) computers to operate equipment and monitor parameters, making necessary adjustments to maintain optimal performance.

  • Compliance & Safety Oversight: Ensure strict adherence to all local, State, and Federal regulations, as well as internal plant procedures.

  • Hazardous Materials & Security: Maintain plant security, handle and transfer bulk chemicals, and ensure safe storage and transport of waste materials.

  • Chemical Analysis: Perform chemical analysis and control on steam, cooling, and condensate systems, while meticulously maintaining chemistry logs.

  • Lockout Tagout (LOTO): Utilize RedTag PRO and other specialized software for the professional issuance of Lockout Tagouts to ensure personnel safety during maintenance.

  • Technical Troubleshooting: Resolve the most complex technical issues and independently prioritize responsibilities for specific functional areas.

  • Process Improvement: Assist in the development of Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and provide strategic input to enhance plant efficiency, reliability, and safety.

  • Training & Mentorship: Provide advanced on-the-job skills training to others in complex technical areas and guide team members in task completion.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Experience: Generally 10+ years of directly related experience in a power plant environment.

  • Specialized Knowledge: Deep understanding of health and safety regulations, including working around hazardous energy, chemicals, and waste materials.

  • Technical Skills: Previous experience using test equipment, calibration appliances, and machinery repair/control systems.

  • Aptitude: Strong mechanical aptitude with a basic understanding of chemistry, physics, electricity, and mathematics.

  • Decision Making: Proven ability to make competent decisions regarding non-routine technical issues and emergency operations.

  • Computer Proficiency: Skilled in using PC computers, Microsoft Office products, and specialized plant control software.

  • Physical Capabilities: Ability to perform walking, reaching, climbing, stooping, and lifting up to 50 pounds.

  • Authorization: Must be authorized to work in the USA.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

Bonus Points:

  • Advanced Education: Degree from a technical or vocational school, or relevant military service.

  • Certifications: Possession of advanced certifications or licensures relevant to power plant operations.

  • Equipment Operation: Experience operating heavy equipment such as manlifts and forklifts.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $50 -$58/HR + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

title: Postdoctoral Fellow-MSH-32910-036
description:
Description

Postdoctoral Fellow — Human Genomics

Position Overview

We are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Fellow with extensive experience in statistical genetics/genetic epidemiology to join our research program focused on the genetics and genomics of complex traits and rare disorders under the supervision of Dr. Nathalie Chami.

Our research integrates large-scale human genetic and genomic data with electronic health records, proteomics, multi-omics, and other deeply phenotyped datasets to understand the genetic architecture and biological heterogeneity of complex disease. A major focus of the lab is moving beyond gene discovery to understand disease penetrance, subtypes, mechanisms, and comorbidities, with the long-term goal of advancing precision medicine.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to lead projects using large, diverse biobanks and population-based cohorts, including datasets with genome-wide genotyping, whole-exome and whole-genome sequencing, longitudinal electronic health records, proteomics, and other molecular and clinical phenotypes.

The position is particularly well suited for a candidate interested in developing an independent research program in human genetics, statistical genetics, genetic epidemiology, or computational genomics.

Research Areas

Potential research areas include:

  • Genetic discovery for obesity, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and related cardiometabolic traits
  • Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and fine-mapping
  • Rare-variant association analyses using whole-exome and whole-genome sequencing
  • Integration of rare and common genetic variation
  • Polygenic risk scores and genetic modifiers of disease penetrance
  • Genetic and molecular characterization of disease subtypes
  • Multi-ancestry and cross-population genetic analyses
  • Integration of genomics with proteomics and other multi-omics data
  • Genetics of longitudinal clinical outcomes and electronic health record-derived phenotypes
  • Integration of genomic and imaging-derived traits
  • Causal inference and translation of genetic discoveries into biological and clinical insight

Responsibilities

Responsibilities

The Postdoctoral Fellow will:

  • Lead independent research projects from study design through analysis, interpretation, and publication
  • Analyze large-scale genomic datasets, including GWAS, exome sequencing, whole-genome sequencing, and rare-variant data
  • Integrate genomic data with clinical, EHR, proteomic, multi-omic, and other phenotypic datasets
  • Develop and implement rigorous statistical and computational approaches for human genetic studies
  • Interpret genetic findings in the context of disease biology and potential clinical relevance
  • Prepare manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals and present findings at national and international scientific meetings
  • Contribute to grant applications and development of new research directions
  • Collaborate with investigators across genetics, epidemiology, clinical medicine, bioinformatics, data science, and related disciplines

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Candidates should have:

  • A PhD in human genetics, statistical genetics, genetic epidemiology, bioinformatics, computational biology, biostatistics, or a closely related field
  • Strong quantitative and analytical skills
  • Experience analyzing human genetic or genomic data
  • Proficiency in R
  • Experience working in Unix/Linux computational environments
  • Strong understanding of statistical principles relevant to genetic and epidemiologic research
  • Ability to independently analyze data, critically interpret results, and troubleshoot analytical problems
  • Strong scientific writing and communication skills
  • Demonstrated ability to work both independently and collaboratively
  • Experience in statistical genetic including GWAS , Whole-exome or whole-genome sequencing analysis
  • Polygenic risk scores
  • Fine-mapping, colocalization, or other post-GWAS analyses
  • Large-scale biobank datasets
  • High-performance computing and reproducible computational workflows
  • A strong publication record and evidence of the ability to take scientific ownership of a project are highly valued.

Desired Attributes

We are looking for someone who is:

  • Scientifically curious and creative
  • Highly motivated and intellectually independent
  • Interested in asking biologically and clinically meaningful questions using human genomic data
  • Rigorous and thoughtful in quantitative analysis
  • Proactive and able to move projects forward independently
  • Collaborative and comfortable working in multidisciplinary teams
  • Organized, dependable, and committed to reproducible research
  • Interested in developing toward scientific independence

Research Environment and Career Development

The fellow will work in a highly collaborative environment at the intersection of human genetics, genomics, epidemiology, computational biology, and precision medicine. The position provides access to large-scale genomic and deeply phenotyped datasets and opportunities to collaborate with investigators across multiple disciplines.

A major emphasis will be placed on the fellow’s career development and scientific independence. Fellows will be encouraged to develop their own research questions, lead manuscripts, present their work at scientific meetings, participate in grant writing, and pursue fellowship and career-development funding.

Application Materials

Interested candidates should submit:

  • Curriculum vitae
  • Brief cover letter describing research experience and future research interests
  • Contact information for 2–3 references

title: Foundation and Corporate Grant Writer
description:
Summary

Epworth Children & Family Services is seeking a Foundation and Corporate Grant Writer who enjoys writing, researching, and translating complex programs into clear, compelling narratives that drive funding.

The Foundation and Corporate Grant Writer leads Epworth’s private foundation and corporate grant portfolio, developing proposals and reports while managing the administrative processes that keep grant work organized and on track.

This position collaborates closely with the Chief Development Officer, Grants Manager, Program teams, and Finance to develop accurate, compelling, and timely submissions that align with organizational priorities and funder requirements.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys persuasive writing, thoughtful research, and the project management required to move strong proposals from idea to submission.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Research private foundation and corporate funding opportunities aligned with Epworth’s programs, priorities, and funding needs.
  • Manage assigned foundation and corporate grants from prospect research through submission and reporting.
  • Develop clear, compelling narratives that connect community need, program delivery, measurable outcomes, organizational impact, and funder priorities.
  • Gather program information, outcomes, stories, budgets, and supporting documentation in collaboration with Program, Finance, and Development staff.
  • Maintain application, reporting, and administrative deadlines in Instrumental.
  • Maintain complete and organized grant files, including applications, reports, agreements, correspondence, budgets, and supporting documentation.
  • Ensure required attachments and supporting documents are accurate, current, organized, and submission-ready.
  • Maintain accurate records in Instrumental of grant submissions, reports, decisions, awards, deadlines, and other relevant activity.
  • Participate in shared proposal review, editing, and quality assurance across the grants team.
  • Partner with the Development Communications Manager to identify stories, outcomes, and program information that can support broader organizational storytelling.
  • Communicate proactively when information, approvals, program data, or other materials needed to meet deadlines are missing or delayed.
  • Perform other grant-related responsibilities consistent with the scope and level of the position.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred, but direct grant writing experience will be valued highly if an HS Diploma is the highest level of education
  • 2+ years of experience in nonprofit communications or grant writing
  • Experience gathering information from multiple stakeholders and synthesizing into a cohesive narrative
  • Experience with CRM systems (Raiser’s Edge or similar preferred)
  • Strong writing and editing skills with the ability to simplify complex information and communicate clearly and persuasively
  • Strong attention to detail
  • Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across teams
  • Passion for advancing the mission of Epworth Children & Family Services

Core Competencies:

  • Clear & Persuasive Writing
  • Project Management
  • Attention to Detail
  • Data Collection & Accuracy

What Success Looks Like in this Position:

  • 100% of grant proposals submitted on time
  • Strong, clear narratives that reflect Epworth’s programs and impact
  • Accurate and timely grant reports with no compliance issues
  • Grant data is consistently accurate across systems, with no discrepancies between CRM, tracker, and submitted applications
  • Effective collaboration across Development, Programs, and Finance

Application Process:

Candidates selected for an interview will be asked to provide a portfolio of prior work.

Sample materials may include:

  • Grant proposals or excerpts
  • Long-form communications
  • Outcomes reporting
  • Logic models

All applicants are required to pass a background check prior to employment to ensure the safety of the youth we serve.

Physical Demands: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to communicate effectively. The physical requirements of this job include: sitting, standing, walking, and climbing stairs on a regular basis; lifting up to 25lbs, pulling and/or pushing on occasion.

Work Environment: Most of the work for this position is performed under normal office conditions. The employee may need to travel from one location to another on an as-needed basis. Employee is required to have reliable personal transportation. Employee may be asked to transport donors, volunteers, and others in a personal vehicle and will be reimbursed for mileage at the current agency rate.
